tracks.description:
This Masterclass will be held before the Odoo Experience Event, over two days, Tuesday, September 22nd and Wednesday, September 23rd, from 9:00 AM to 5:00 PM. Entrance to the Masterclass includes breakfast, lunch, and drinks during both days.
Who is for?
Participants should already be familiar with Odoo’s Inventory, Purchase, and Barcode apps, as well as  be comfortable with supply chain management concepts. This training is not intended for beginners but rather for intermediate level.
Why Attend?
If you're already using the Purchase, Inventory, and Barcode applications but feel you're not fully leveraging their capabilities, the Inventory Masterclass is essential for unlocking the potential of these tools.

The training will be conducted in Odoo 20, providing an opportunity to explore the new features.
Don't miss this opportunity to enhance your skills and boost your efficiency!

tracks.description:

System Navigation: Optimizing the interface for high-efficiency business operations.

Take complete command of your Odoo platform. Join us and become a Studio Expert.

tracks.title: Zero-Click Gmail Integration for Odoo CRM: Fully Automated Email Logging
tracks.speaker: Simon Stappen
tracks.speaker_raw: Simon Stappen, Managing Partner  at Much. Consulting
tracks.speaker_bio: Simon Stappen is the Managing Partner and Founder of much. Consulting, an Odoo Gold Partner. With a background in process automation and digital strategy, Simon has led dozens of complex Odoo implementations focused on maximizing usability and efficiency. He specializes in integrating third-party tools like Gmail to create seamless, user-friendly ERP ecosystems that drive real business value.
tracks.description:
This talk will unveil a powerful Gmail integration for Odoo that revolutionizes how businesses handle email communication in their CRM and beyond. Unlike the standard Gmail-to-Odoo sync, which relies on manual user intervention and unpredictable behaviors, this integration is designed for complete automation. It operates silently in the background, continuously scanning relevant Gmail accounts, intelligently matching emails with Odoo records (e.g., leads, opportunities, partners, tasks), and logging communication threads without requiring any clicks or user confirmation. The result: sales teams, project managers, and customer support agents can work entirely in Odoo, confident that every client interaction is tracked, centralized, and accessible — without the usual overhead.
We'll dive into the technical architecture, show the smart matching logic (e.g., by email address, subject tokens, thread detection), and cover real-world implementation tips. This approach is ideal for organizations aiming to enhance CRM transparency, streamline workflows, and reduce manual data entry.
Key Points:
- Why the standard Gmail sync isn’t good enough: gaps, manual steps, and risks
- Designing a true zero-click email integration for CRM, Helpdesk, Projects
- How matching logic works: intelligent threading, fallback strategies, contact recognition
- Architecture overview: Google APIs, cron jobs, Odoo models, and custom logic
- Deployment insights: access security, scalability, and performance tips
- Real-world results: reduced time-to-update, full conversation visibility, user adoption gains
Key Learnings:
- How to architect a background sync that is reliable, scalable, and fully automated
- Best practices for linking emails to Odoo objects with high accuracy
- How to handle edge cases like shared inboxes, aliases, and partial matches
- The hidden costs of manual CRM email management (and how to eliminate them)
- Boosting user satisfaction and CRM hygiene through invisible automation
Target Audience:
- CRM Managers and Admins seeking better user adoption and data accuracy
- Sales and Customer Support Leaders wanting full communication visibility
- Odoo Developers and Integrators looking to build or improve external email connectors
- Business Owners and Decision Makers evaluating CRM usability and ROI
<div

tracks.title: From POS to Pocket: Extending Odoo to Your Customers
tracks.speaker: Eric Friedlingstein
tracks.speaker_role: Founder & Odoo Solution Architect at Synapsis-Group
tracks.speaker_raw: Eric Friedlingstein, Founder & Odoo Solution Architect at Synapsis-Group
tracks.speaker_bio: Eric Friedlingstein is a Senior Software Architect, Team Leader, and Odoo Certified expert with an M.Sc. in Computer Science. As the founder of Synapsis-Group (est. 1989), he has been leading digital transformation initiatives for over three decades. An official Odoo Partner since 2024, Eric combines deep technical expertise with extensive experience in web and mobile solutions. His talks showcase real-world customer projects and demonstrate how Odoo can be extended beyond traditional ERP boundaries to solve everyday business challenges through practical, user-centered innovation.
tracks.description:
Short description
Discover how a Belgian bar transformed Odoo into a complete customer engagement platform through a native mobile application featuring daily specials, loyalty rewards, push notifications, and customer feedback.
Abstract
For many restaurants, Odoo starts with the Point of Sale. But what if it could also become the platform that keeps customers coming back?
This talk presents the real-life implementation of a customer-facing mobile application developed for Le Caberdouche, a famous Belgian bar that recently migrated its operations to Odoo.
Instead of relying on multiple third-party services for customer communication, loyalty management, and customer feedback, everything is managed natively inside Odoo.
The mobile application allows customers to:
• Receive weekly and daily specials through push notifications
• Collect loyalty points and redeem rewards
• Review and provide instant feedback
• Stay connected through a simple and intuitive mobile experience
Behind the scenes, Odoo becomes the single source of truth for both restaurant operations and customer engagement.
During this 20-minute session, we will demonstrate:
• How Odoo powers a modern native mobile application
• How push notifications increase customer engagement and repeat visits
• How loyalty programs can be fully integrated without external services
• How customer reviews collected directly inside Odoo provide valuable business insights
• Lessons learned while designing a mobile experience that customers actually enjoy using
• How a single Odoo backend powers both business operations and customer engagement
This session demonstrates how Odoo can evolve from an ERP into a complete customer engagement platform, helping hospitality businesses strengthen customer relationships, increase customer loyalty, and deliver a seamless digital experience.
<div

tracks.title: Ditching the Patchwork: A Biotech Startup's Bet on Odoo
tracks.speaker: Béla Surányi & Balázs Boga
tracks.speaker_role: Principal Consultant & Co-Founder (COO) at FF Advisors & Microbiom Center
tracks.speaker_raw: Béla Surányi & Balázs Boga, Principal Consultant & Co-Founder (COO) at FF Advisors & Microbiom Center
tracks.speaker_bio: Béla Surányi is a family business advisor who works with companies across Eastern Europe as they navigate ownership succession and digital transformation. He helps founders and next gen leaders modernize operations, replace fragmented tools with integrated systems, and prepare their firms for an AI driven economy. He advised Microbiom Center, Romania’s first clinic dedicated exclusively to the microbiome, on its move to Odoo. His focus is on practical, lasting change that teams can own themselves, rather than depending on an external developer for every adjustment.
tracks.description:
Microbiom Center in Târgu Mureș is the first clinic in Romania dedicated exclusively to the human microbiome, founded by a second generation Romanian entrepreneurial family.
Like many young firms in the region, the team started with a patchwork of tools: a WordPress site, a medical booking plugin, and several disconnected applications. Every change depended on an outside developer, which made the operation slow and costly.
This talk tells the story of the move to Odoo and what changed once a single platform replaced that patchwork.
The clinic now runs CRM, online booking with a book and pay later option, the website connected to a patient portal, a detailed patient database, full inventory linked to sales, invoicing with Romanian E-Factura, vendor bills, financial reconciliation, leave management, and email marketing inside one system. Invoicing and reminders are automated, and every test is traceable through the inventory module. The owners and team now make changes on their own and gain value from each new Odoo release.
The session also frames a wider pattern: many Eastern European firms founded in the 1990s face a triple transition at once: real operational digitalization, a generational handover of ownership, and a shift toward an AI driven economy.
Drawing on the speaker’s work as a family business advisor, the talk shows how an integrated ERP can carry a company through all three.
Key learnings: why unifying the stack beats stitching together point solutions, ⁠how to move a team from developer dependency to self sufficiency, and ⁠how integrated modules compound in value for a biotech operation.
Target audience: founders, ⁠family business owners, ⁠operators, ⁠advisors, and ⁠Odoo partners working with companies in transition.
<div

tracks.title: €600 Billion Black Hole: The Keys to Modeling an Invisible Market
tracks.speaker: Amaury Marescaux
tracks.speaker_raw: Amaury Marescaux, CEO at Gondola Foodservice
tracks.description:
Out-of-home food and beverage consumption (Restaurants, cafés & bars, corporate canteens, fuel station stores) is worth more than €600 billion a year in Europe, and almost none of it is measured. Gondola Foodservice's mission is to model that black hole. Amaury, founder and CEO, looks back at why they succeeded early on, and what you can take away from it.

tracks.title: Rethinking the Energy Transition
tracks.speaker: Stefan Grosjean
tracks.speaker_role: Founder & CEO of Smappee/ Snowball at Smappee/ Snowball
tracks.speaker_raw: Stefan Grosjean, Founder & CEO of Smappee/ Snowball at Smappee/ Snowball
tracks.speaker_bio:
Stefan Grosjean (°1963) grew up in Flanders, Belgium, and earned a Master of Science in Industrial Engineering, specializing in Computer Science and Electronics. In 1991, Stefan founded EnergyICT, a pioneering company in energy solutions for commercial and industrial businesses. Over the next two decades, EnergyICT became a global leader in energy management technologies, laying the foundation for Stefan’s reputation as a visionary in the clean-tech industry. He sold the company in 2009.
Building on this success, in 2012 Stefan founded Smappee, an innovative company that focuses on optimizing energy consumption and accelerating the transition to renewable energy. Smappee is internationally recognized for its intelligent EV chargers and smart energy management solutions, which blend functionality with sleek design. Under his leadership, Smappee has won numerous prestigious awards, including the Henry Van De Velde Award, the Red Dot Award, and the iF Design Award. As of October 2024, Stefan transitioned to the role of CEO of Smappee Group, the umbrella body over the various Smappee ventures. In this new role, he remains closely involved in Smappee's management but with a sharpened focus on the visionary innovation and strategy of the Group to ensure Smappee's accelerated growth and leading position in the industry.
In addition to his role at Smappee, Stefan founded  Snowball in 2018, a cutting-edge Cleantech Hub in Harelbeke. Snowball serves as the headquarters of Smappee and acts as a collaborative space and living lab for clean-tech innovation, bringing together companies and experts focused on sustainable energy and environmental solutions.
With over 30 years of experience, Stefan is a recognized leader in the global energy transition, consistently striving to blend cutting-edge technology with high-functioning design and sustainable growth strategies. His passion for innovation and commitment to positive societal and environmental impact continue to drive his entrepreneurial ventures.
tracks.description:
The energy transition is changing how we generate, store and use energy. But unlocking its full potential requires more than renewable energy alone. It requires intelligence.
In this keynote,  Stefan Grosjean, Founder & CEO of Smappee , shares his vision for a smarter energy future, shaped by more than three decades of entrepreneurship and innovation. Through personal insights and lessons learned, he explores how intelligent energy management can help create a more flexible, connected and sustainable energy system.
An inspiring perspective on energy, technology and the power of thinking differently combined with a clear view on the future.

tracks.title: Changer de dimension sans perdre sa trajectoire
tracks.speaker: Kévin Petit
tracks.speaker_raw: Kévin Petit, Pilote automobile professionnel
tracks.description:
À plus de 200 km/h, la moindre prise de décision se joue à la milliseconde. Passer un cap, monter de catégorie ou viser plus haut demande de se réinventer sans jamais concéder sur ce qui fait sa force.
Au travers d’un récit captivant au cœur du sport automobile de haut niveau, Kévin Petit partage sa vision du dépassement de soi. Comment garder le cap face aux virages imprévus ? Comment accélérer son développement personnel et professionnel sans sacrifier ses valeurs fondamentales ?
Une conférence inspirante, riche en parallèles poignants entre la piste et l’entreprenariat, qui vous donnera les clés pour accepter le changement, performer sous pression et tracer votre propre voie vers l’excellence

tracks.title: Untangling Excise Duties: Managing Bonded Wine & Spirits Warehousing in Odoo Standard
tracks.speaker: Julien Brunin & Samy Brahimi
tracks.speaker_role: CEO et Business Analyst at Acsone
tracks.speaker_raw: Julien Brunin & Samy Brahimi, CEO et Business Analyst at Acsone
tracks.speaker_bio: Sera fournir à la confirmation du talk.
tracks.description:
With over a century of history, Les Vins Brunin-Guiller is a major actor in wine and spirits retail, import, and export across Belgium and France. But behind every fine bottle lies a complex web of customs regulations, bonded warehouses (hors douane), and excise duties.
Unlike standard taxes like VAT, excise taxes in the alcohol sector are triggered at a very specific and critical moment: when the product leaves the tax-suspended customs regime (hors douane) and is cleared for domestic market distribution. Managing this dual-status inventory and ensuring tax compliance across purchases, internal transfers, and sales is a notorious nightmare for wine merchants.
In this talk, we will reveal how we successfully implemented a fully compliant, integrated flow for Vins Brunin-Guiller. You will discover how we leveraged Odoo Standard—using multi-warehouses, specific route configurations, and native inventory features—to automate excise tax calculations and track every stock movement from purchase to final delivery.
What you will learn (Key Takeaways):
- Bonded vs. Duty-Paid Flows: How to design a seamless multi-warehouse and location structure in Odoo to manage tax-suspended (hors douane) and tax-paid stocks.
- Automating Excise Triggers: How to capture the exact moment excise duties must be applied during stock moves, minimizing human error and audit risks.
- The Power of Standard: Practical tips and tricks to solve complex regulatory and localization issues using Odoo’s native features, avoiding heavy custom developments.
- Real-world Feedback: Lessons learned from a century-old business transitioning to a modern, integrated ERP.

tracks.title: Choosing Odoo Over SAP: The 10-Year Transformation Journey of a Global Pharmaceutical Group
tracks.speaker: Amit Parik
tracks.speaker_raw: Amit Parik, Managing Partner at BrowseInfo
tracks.speaker_bio:
My name is Amit Parik, and I am the Managing Partner at BrowseInfo, an Odoo Gold Partner that has been providing Odoo services since 2013. Before starting BrowseInfo, I worked at Odoo (formerly OpenERP), which gave me deep insight into the product, roadmap, and best practices for successful implementations.
At BrowseInfo, we focus on business consulting and end‑to‑end Odoo implementation, not just development. As a long‑standing Gold Partner, we help customers with process analysis, solution design, configuration, customisation, integrations, training, support, and continuous improvement on Odoo. Over the years, I have led and overseen 100+ Odoo implementations across India and around the world in industries such as pharma, manufacturing, trading, services, retail, NGOs, education, and temples.
BrowseInfo is also known in the Odoo ecosystem for its large portfolio of ready‑to‑use Odoo apps and vertical solutions on the Odoo Apps store, which partners and end customers use to accelerate their projects and reduce custom development.
One of my flagship projects is with Sasmar Pharmaceuticals, a global pharma group that has been on Odoo for more than a decade. Starting from Odoo 7 and now on Odoo 19 Enterprise, we supported Sasmar’s growth from 6 to 22 companies across multiple countries, with Odoo as the backbone for ERP, eCommerce, multi‑website, and marketplace integrations. This long‑term journey has given me strong experience in multi‑company, multi‑currency architectures, complex rollouts, and multi‑version upgrades, turning Odoo into a true core system for international businesses.
tracks.description:
In 2014, Sasmar Pharmaceuticals faced a critical strategic decision.
Operating across multiple countries with growing manufacturing, distribution, and eCommerce operations, the company evaluated traditional enterprise ERP platforms, including SAP, to support its next phase of international growth. Instead, Sasmar selected Odoo (formerly OpenERP), a decision that would shape the next decade of its business transformation.
Today, Sasmar operates 22 companies across Europe, Asia-Pacific, North America, and Latin America, with Odoo serving as the digital backbone of its global operations.
This session is not a software implementation story. It is a business transformation case study.
We will explore how Sasmar evolved from a group of 6 companies into a globally integrated pharmaceutical organization while maintaining a single ERP strategy, standardized operating model, and unified data architecture. Attendees will gain insight into the governance, scalability, and architectural decisions that enabled rapid international expansion without the complexity and fragmentation commonly associated with multinational growth.
The session will cover:
* The ERP evaluation process and why Sasmar selected Odoo over traditional enterprise alternatives.
* Designing an ERP architecture for future expansion rather than current requirements.
* Building a centralized multi-company, multi-currency, and multi-warehouse operating model.
* Supporting manufacturing, supply chain, finance, and commercial operations across multiple countries.
* Managing more than 25 Shopify stores, Amazon channels, websites, and digital commerce operations through a unified platform.
* The evolution from Odoo 7 to Odoo 19 and lessons learned from a decade of continuous innovation and upgrades.
* Governance frameworks, customization strategies, and scalability principles that enabled long-term success.
More importantly, we will share what worked, what failed, what we would do differently today, and the practical lessons organizations can apply when building a long-term ERP roadmap.
For CEOs, CFOs, COOs, CIOs, ERP leaders, and growing international businesses, this session demonstrates how Odoo can move beyond departmental automation to become a strategic platform for global expansion.
Ten years ago, Sasmar chose Odoo as an ERP system.
A decade later, it has become the foundation that supports 22 companies, multiple continents, global manufacturing, digital commerce, and continued growth.
This is the story of how an ERP decision became a business transformation journey.
⸻
Why This Session Matters
Most ERP discussions focus on software features.
This session focuses on what business leaders truly care about:
How do you build an ERP foundation that can support international growth, acquisitions, new markets, digital commerce, and operational complexity for more than a decade without replacing the platform every few years?
Using Sasmar Pharmaceuticals’ real-world journey, attendees will see how strategic ERP decisions, governance, and scalable architecture can enable sustainable global growth while avoiding the costs, disruption, and complexity often associated with large-scale ERP transformations.
⸻
Speaker Perspective
Delivered jointly by the leadership teams of Sasmar Pharmaceuticals and BrowseInfo, sharing over ten years of practical experience scaling one of Odoo’s longest-running global pharmaceutical implementations.

tracks.title: Odoo for Aerospace: Enforcing No-Fly Zones in the Warehouse
tracks.speaker: Bernhard Hilfer
tracks.speaker_raw: Bernhard Hilfer,  ERP Consultant  at much. Consulting
tracks.speaker_bio: Bernhard Hilfer is a manufacturing-focused ERP Consultant at much. Consulting, dedicated to helping mid-sized companies optimize their production inside Odoo Enterprise.
tracks.description:
In aerospace manufacturing, storing a standard prototype in a restricted "Flight-Critical" zone is not merely an operational error; it is a severe compliance breach that jeopardizes safety certifications and audit status. Managing this across complex bills of materials requires infallible, automated segregation of physical inventory based on strict component compliance levels.
To solve this, we expanded the Odoo Enterprise Inventory and Barcode apps to engineer a rigid "Compliance Flag" setup. By binding specific compliance attributes directly to Serial Numbers and Stock Locations, the system enforces a strict key-lock matching rule during every internal stock move. If a warehouse operator attempts to scan a non-compliant part into a restricted zone, it instantly triggers a hard stop within the Odoo Barcode interface, preventing the transaction.
As a result, zone mistakes dropped to absolute zero. Automating these checks during scanning also cut manual quality assurance time by 40%, keeping warehouse operations fast without sacrificing safety. Attendees will discover the exact data model changes, the barcode logic setup, and practical lessons for enforcing strict compliance in a busy warehouse environment.
Key Points of this Talk:
- Data Model Extension: Extending standard Odoo Serial Number and Stock Location models to support unique compliance attributes.
- Key-Lock Matching Logic: Engineering strict validation rules that pair component safety flags directly with destination zone restrictions.
- Real-Time Barcode Enforcement: Configuring automated hard stops inside the Odoo Barcode UI to block incorrect physical scans instantly.
- Preventing Segregation Breaches: How the system physically keeps non-compliant aerospace parts out of secure storage areas.
- Fallback Handling: Executing smart routing logic to guide standard inventory to regular shelves without breaking warehouse workflows.
Key Learnings:
- How to enforce strict Serial-to-Location validation in Odoo Enterprise Inventory.
- How to trigger hard validation stops in the Enterprise Barcode UI.
- How to architect scalable compliance rules for highly regulated industries.
Target Audience:
Supply Chain Directors, QA Managers, and Technical Consultants using Odoo Enterprise.

tracks.title: Building Heat Treatment Plants in Odoo: Automating ETO Manufacturing with 20,000 BoMs
tracks.speaker: Nadja Planic
tracks.speaker_role: Head of Manufacturing ERP Consulting at much. Consulting
tracks.speaker_raw: Nadja Planic, Head of Manufacturing ERP Consulting at much. Consulting
tracks.speaker_bio: Nadja Planic is the Head of Manufacturing ERP Consulting at much. Consulting. She leads the team focusing on the conception, implementation, and optimization of ERP projects. Nadja has extensive expertise with compliance and quality topics in Odoo, leading projects for manufacturing-heavy companies with highly compliance-sensitive processes, ensuring they meet stringent industry standards.
tracks.description:
In Engineering-to-Order (ETO) manufacturing, the transition from design to production often breaks down when teams rely on disconnected spreadsheets. Kohnle, a manufacturer of industrial heat treatment plants, experienced this firsthand. They managed a large catalog of 45,000 products and 20,000 Bills of Materials (BoMs) using manual cost calculations in Excel and static quotes in Word. These media breaks forced the team into time-consuming data re-entry, causing procurement errors that directly threatened project timelines.
To resolve this, we consolidated their entire engineering and manufacturing logic into Odoo Enterprise, utilizing Analytical Accounting and PLM to enforce a rigid "Release-to-Manufacture" process and cost control.
Additionally, with automatic task creation and bidirectional data synchronization from Manufacturing Orders into the Project App, we transformed static manufacturing data into dynamic project milestones. This architecture allows Kohnle to manage dependencies and resource planning within the Odoo Gantt view, providing a real-time overview of their complex engineering projects.
Key Points of the Talk:
- Leaving Spreadsheets Behind: How Kohnle moved 45,000 products and 20,000 BoMs from fragmented media into one unified system.
- Structuring the Engineering Handover: How we implemented Odoo BoM releases to create a clear process for sending designs to production.
- Connecting Production to Planning: Automatically creating Project Tasks from Manufacturing Orders to keep long-term schedules up to date.
- Building Digital Guardrails: Enforcing data integrity via granular access rights during cross-department handovers.
- Closing the Gaps: Eliminating manual media breaks between cost calculation, quoting, and production execution.
Key Learnings:
- How to bridge the functional gap between PLM engineering and MRP production.
- How to automate project-based manufacturing using Odoo’s native task-sync logic.
- How to manage large-scale data migrations without losing BoM hierarchy.
- How to configure Odoo Enterprise to handle complex ETO timeline dependencies.
Target Audience:
- Operations Managers and CTOs in Engineering/Manufacturing.
- Project Leads managing complex ETO cycles in Odoo Enterprise.
- Functional Consultants specialized in PLM and MRP integrations.

tracks.title: How to build a project agreement framework in Odoo for complex wholesale distribution
tracks.speaker: Tânia Manco
tracks.speaker_raw: Tânia Manco, ERP Consultant at much. Consulting
tracks.speaker_bio: Tânia Manco is a Consultant at much. Consulting, specializing in Odoo implementations for the commerce sectors across the DACH region. With a deep understanding of the Odoo stack Tânia excels at bridging the gap between complex business requirements and scalable technical architecture.
tracks.description:
Construction wholesale is built on long-term, multi-partner B2B projects. Standard Odoo handles sales and procurement well, but the specific demands of such complex supply chains require a more tailored approach. Managing project-level pricing, dual delivery methods (dropship vs. warehouse), and contracts across dozens of subcontractors requires stepping outside the standard setup. This talk explores how to build an "Agreement Framework" that connects these moving parts into one unified process.
Key Points of the Talk:
- Find the Gap: Identifying where out-of-the-box Odoo features like blanket orders and pricelists reach their limits in complex distribution scenarios.
- The Agreement Framework: Designing a central model that links sales and purchasing, tracks quantities in real time, and automates price inheritance.
- Live Demo: A walkthrough of creating an agreement, comparing margins between delivery routes, and watching child orders automatically update project balances.
- Architecture & Logic: The reasoning behind our technical choices, specifically how we handled unit of measure conversions and automated margin calculations.
- The Future: A brief look at upcoming Odoo features and why a dedicated orchestration layer will still matter for specialized industries.
Key Learnings:
- Why building a dedicated "Agreement" model is more stable than extending standard sales or purchase orders.
- How to store "Dropship vs. Warehouse" prices for the same agreement to enable easy comparisons.
- Lessons learned from aggregating real-time data across various stages of the supply chain.
- The importance of allowing agreements to apply to product groups, not just individual SKUs, to handle substitutions.
- Why secondary units of measure and custom order states must be part of the initial architecture, not an afterthought.
Target Audience:
- Functional Consultants & Developers looking for ways to extend Odoo for complex trading and distribution.
- IT Leads & Project Managers at companies dealing with multi-partner agreements or intricate B2B pricing.

tracks.title: Stop Writing AI Prompts by Hand: Building a Self-Fixing Native AI Loop in Odoo 19
tracks.speaker: Mike Schulz
tracks.speaker_role: Senior Expert ERP Consultant  at much. Consulting
tracks.speaker_raw: Mike Schulz, Senior Expert ERP Consultant  at much. Consulting
tracks.speaker_bio: Mike Schulz is a Senior Expert ERP Consultant at much. Consulting, an Odoo Gold Partner, with offices in Germany, Portugal, and the UK. He helps companies of all sizes to drive growth and improve business processes with innovative Odoo Solutions. Mike is an expert in process automation and digital strategy, having successfully implemented countless Odoo projects to streamline operations and enhance efficiency.
tracks.description:
Static AI prompts lose accuracy quickly as new business edge cases pop up, forcing admins to constantly rewrite them. When routing Helpdesk tickets or scoring CRM leads, the AI often guesses wrong. Users fix these mistakes daily, but the system forgets the corrections, forcing people to fix the same errors over and over.
To solve this, we built a two-agent system that learns from its mistakes, using only standard Odoo Enterprise v19 AI features. We set this up entirely using Odoo Studio and server actions—no custom Python code required. When a user changes an AI-generated field—like fixing a wrong ticket priority—a second background AI immediately notices the change. This second AI looks at why the user made the change and automatically rewrites the first AI's instructions so it gets it right the next time.
By feeding human corrections directly back into the system, we completely stopped writing AI prompts by hand in our testing environment. This setup matches AI outputs directly to real human actions, allowing CRM and Helpdesk automation to run without constant admin upkeep.
Key Points of this Talk:
- Set up two-part AI loops using built-in Odoo Enterprise v19 AI functions.
- Record manual field changes to trigger background AI updates.
- Use Odoo Studio to automate AI prompt changes without custom Python code.
- Build server actions to update AI prompts automatically on the fly.
- Apply self-correcting loops to CRM lead scoring and Helpdesk ticket routing.
Key Learnings:
- How to build an AI loop that fixes itself using Odoo Enterprise v19 features.
- How to use manual field edits to train a background AI assistant.
- How to stop writing AI prompts by hand using Odoo server actions.
- How to use Odoo Studio to manage multi-step AI setups.
Target Audience:

tracks.title: Setting Up Odoo for Long-Term Rental: Products, Contracts & Automated recurring Billing

Key takeaways include: how to configure products specifically for LTR use cases, which invoicing settings have the biggest impact on billing accuracy, and how to handle common edge cases such as contract renewals, early terminations, and prorated periods.
The value for the audience lies in understanding the full functional chain — not just isolated settings — and walking away with a clear, battle-tested configuration blueprint ready to apply in real projects.

tracks.title: How to streamline the unavoidable in E-Commerce: fully integrated and highly automated returns processing with Odoo
tracks.speaker: Iva Shtembari
tracks.speaker_role: Full Stack Consultant at bobco GmbH
tracks.speaker_raw: Iva Shtembari, Full Stack Consultant at bobco GmbH
tracks.speaker_bio: Iva is a Full Stack Consultant at bobco GmbH, a Berlin-based ERP agency specializing in Odoo implementations for high-growth e-commerce and operationally complex companies. Iva's work focuses on turning messy real-world operations into clean, maintainable Odoo workflows.
tracks.description:
Most e-commerce teams think of returns as a warehouse process. A product comes back, a return transfer is validated, and inventory is updated.
But at scale, that is only a small part of the story.
A real return touches customer service, warehouse operations, accounting, payments, eCom, helpdesk, inventory valuation, refund rules, restocking fees, scrapping, and exception handling. If those steps are spread across multiple screens and manual decisions, returns become slow, error-prone, and frustrating for both customers and internal teams.
In this talk, I’ll show how we designed a scalable return workflow in Odoo for high-volume e-commerce operations. The pattern starts with a simple idea: use return categories as the operational decision point. From there, Odoo can decide whether to create a normal return, scrap products immediately, auto-create credit memos, apply restocking fees, trigger Shopify refunds, or route exceptions to the right team.
This talk is about designing the full after-sales loop in Odoo: return intake, warehouse processing, refund accounting, payment execution, and exception management.
What you’ll learn:
- Why returns should be modeled as an end-to-end after-sales workflow, not just a reverse picking.
- How return categories can drive automation across warehouse, accounting, and customer service.
- How to reduce manual return handling without removing operational control.
- How to design credit memo automation safely, including exclusions, restocking fees, and draft/auto-confirm logic.
- How Shopify refund automation can be connected to posted credit memos.
- Where to use activities, Helpdesk tickets, chatter, and operational views for return exceptions.

tracks.speaker_bio: Bernhard Hilfer is a manufacturing-focused ERP Consultant at much. Consulting, dedicated to helping mid-sized companies optimize their production inside Odoo Enterprise.
tracks.description:
In mid-sized manufacturing, successfully processing deep Bills of Materials depends on flawless dependency scheduling. However, manually scheduling thousands of interdependent Work Orders is practically impossible. The inevitable consequences are a cluttered shop floor overflowing with Work-in-Progress (WIP), hidden bottlenecks, and constantly missed delivery dates. While many companies attempt to solve this chaos through costly integrations with external planning tools, this talk will explore a smarter alternative: building lightweight, highly practical scheduling logic directly into the Odoo Enterprise MRP core.
We will demonstrate how leveraging standard priority flags and deadline fields can automatically schedule operations against actual machine capacity. Running these high-volume calculations takes seconds and immediately populates standard Odoo Gantt views with accurate forecasts.
Attendees will walk away with a deep understanding of how to eliminate friction between the sales desk and the factory floor, easily accommodate rush orders, and guarantee verifiable delivery dates - all without ever leaving their primary ERP system.
Key Points of This Talk:
- The operational impact of deep Bills of Materials on manual scheduling workflows
- Why external third-party planning tools often result in expensive data silos
- Architecture overview: embedding custom heuristic MRP logic directly into Odoo
- Aligning material allocation with machine capacity to drastically reduce physical WIP
- Visualizing high-speed capacity calculations within built-in Odoo Gantt views
- Bridging the gap: achieving operational transparency between sales and production
Key Learnings:
- Understand the technical approach to building custom scheduling logic natively in Odoo
- Learn how to utilize standard MO priority flags and deadlines to drive automated sequencing
- Discover actionable strategies to dynamically manage and schedule high-volume rush orders
- Gain the ability to translate complex production data into clear bottleneck forecasts
- Walk away with a blueprint for securing verifiable sales delivery dates based on realistic machine capacity
Target Audience:
- Manufacturing Consultants and Odoo Integrators expanding their MRP capabilities
- Production Managers targeting Mittelstand operations
- Sales Teams requiring realistic, verifiable delivery forecasting

In this talk, Tim Freudenthal (HLR GmbH) and Reiner Hannaske (Intero Technologies GmbH) provide practical insights into the introduction of Odoo as a central company platform. They will show how Odoo has become the mainstay of day-to-day business with individually customizable rental periods, complex serial number and warehouse management and the documentation of test certificates.
Special attention is paid to the step-by-step approach: from the requirements workshop to MVP implementation and continuous further development - all with one clear goal: efficient, scalable processes in one system. An inspiring experience report for anyone who wants to master industry-specific complexity with digital ease.

tracks.title: Agentic AI-Driven SAP HANA to Odoo Migration at Scale with Zero-Downtime
tracks.speaker: Om Prakash Maurya
tracks.speaker_role: Delivery Head - CRM & ERP at Ksolves IT USA Inc.
tracks.speaker_raw: Om Prakash Maurya, Delivery Head - CRM & ERP at Ksolves IT USA Inc.
tracks.speaker_bio:
Om Prakash Maurya is the Delivery Head - CRM and ERP at Ksolves India Limited, leading a team of 150+ Odoo professionals to ensure successful, high-quality project delivery. With a deep understanding of Odoo, he drives end-to-end execution across diverse industries.
Om specializes in aligning technology with business goals, overseeing solution architecture, resource management, and client satisfaction. His expertise also extends to Kubernetes, DevOps, and server configuration, enabling scalable, efficient deployments. Passionate about innovation and operational excellence, he plays a key role in driving digital transformation for global clients through Odoo and cutting-edge open-source technologies.
tracks.description:
As organizations outgrow the rigidity and rising costs of SAP HANA, Odoo is emerging as the strategic alternative, but migration is rarely straightforward.
This talk reveals how:
- AI intelligently maps SAP HANA data structures, flags field conflicts, and auto-generates assessment reports, dramatically reducing manual analysis effort.
- Agentic AI takes it further by autonomously orchestrating zero-downtime cutovers, continuously scoring migration risk, and escalating issues in real time, compressing go-live timelines to as little as weeks.
- Post-migration agents run autonomously in the background, monitoring data integrity and surfacing reconciliation gaps before they become production incidents, ensuring a smooth transition without requiring constant manual oversight.
Ideal for people and organizations that want to move away from SAP because of escalating costs but remain concerned about losing historical business data, disrupting operations, or undertaking a complex migration.
Key Learnings:
- The hidden cost of staying on SAP HANA, and the ROI case for switching.
- How AI agents compress a months-long migration into weeks without downtime.
- Real pitfalls, honest limitations, and what actually makes a go-live succeed.

tracks.title: Mastering the Payroll Journal Entry with Swiss Compliance
tracks.speaker: Monteiro Da Silva from Sodexis Sàrl
tracks.speaker_raw: Monteiro Da Silva from Sodexis Sàrl
tracks.description:
Are you struggling to keep your financial accounting fully aligned with Switzerland's strict, multi-layered payroll regulations? Navigating the complex ledger requirements for Swiss social security (AVS/AI/APG), occupational pensions (LPP), accidents (AANP), and canton-specific withholding taxes (impôt à la source) presents an ongoing compliance and operational challenge for financial and HR teams alike.
Enter the power of a localized ERP solution! Generating a compliant monthly payroll journal entry no longer requires manual cross-referencing, external spreadsheets, or high-risk manual accounting entries. By establishing a robust, automated bridge between HR payroll structures and the general ledger, businesses operating in Switzerland can seamlessly translate complex salary distributions into perfectly balanced, regulation-compliant financial data.
Over the past few years, numerous organizations operating across Switzerland have partnered with Sodexis to continuously improve their Odoo implementation, streamlining operations to ensure smooth, compliant, and scalable financial growth. Sodexis has successfully implemented customized accounting and payroll configurations to enable the seamless tracking, splitting, and posting of localized social deductions directly within the core operational workflow.
Join this session to discover how to achieve complete accounting peace of mind with Swiss payroll compliance—and learn how the collaborative partnership between your operational teams and Sodexis can deliver an efficient, future-proof roadmap for your financial workflows.
Representing the implementation success will be key members of our finance integration team, alongside Noémie (Nemo) Keller, Director of Operations for Sodexis.
Since 2012, Sodexis has been a full-service Odoo Implementation Partner, with a Consulting and Development team focused on maximizing customers’ ROI and user experience. Sodexis is one of the longest-tenured implementation Odoo Partners in the US and has offices also in Switzerland, France, and Austria. Sodexis brings a wealth of experience and valuable expertise to its clients, having successfully implemented over 175 projects and built hundreds of custom applications.
More info: https://sodexis.com/

tracks.speaker: Abderraouf Ghrissi from Odoo
tracks.speaker_raw: Abderraouf Ghrissi from Odoo
tracks.description:
For years, the Odoo timesheet meant one thing: remember to hit start on a timer, or rebuild your day from memory on Friday afternoon. We replaced that model with the Timesheet Assistant, a passive layer that watches what you actually worked on and lets you confirm it in one click instead of tracking it in real time.

tracks.title: Autonomous Unit Test Generation with an AI Agent Loop: From Untested Code to Reliable Odoo Modules at Scale
tracks.speaker: Sebastian Kühnel Bozzo
tracks.speaker_raw: Sebastian Kühnel Bozzo, Developer at twio.tech AG
tracks.speaker_bio: Sebastian is developer at twio.tech. In his role, he architects and develops robust and scalable Odoo solutions.
tracks.description:
Maintaining reliable unit tests across customized Odoo modules is one of the most time-consuming and neglected parts of development, especially when working across multiple clients, each with their own business logic and edge cases. The result is often fragile codebases, hidden regressions, and costly debugging cycles in production. In this talk, we present a practical approach to tackling this problem using an AI agent loop that assists developers in generating, validating, and refining unit tests directly from real module code. Rather than relying on one-shot AI prompts, we introduce a structured loop that analyzes the module, proposes test coverage, executes tests, and iteratively improves them based on execution feedback until they become more reliable, meaningful, and executable.
In this talk, we will look at:
- How the AI agent loop works in practice
- Why naive AI-generated tests fail in real Odoo environments, and how iterative execution loops solve this problem
- The role of human-in-the-loop validation to ensure the generated tests actually cover meaningful business logic and real-world edge cases
- Common failure cases we encountered, including tests that pass without testing real logic, missing Odoo context and data dependencies, and tests exposing real bugs in production code
- How to integrate this approach into a real development workflow without disrupting existing practices
Key Learnings:
- How to design an AI agent loop that goes beyond simple prompt-based test generation and produces executable, meaningful tests
- Why execution feedback is critical to avoid false positives and useless test coverage
- How to detect and fix common issues in AI-generated tests, including missing context, weak assertions, and misleading “green” tests
- Why human validation remains critical when generating tests for complex business logic and custom Odoo implementations
Intended Target Audience:
- Odoo developers, technical leads, and consultants who work with custom modules and want to improve code reliability without dramatically increasing development overhead.
It is particularly relevant to:
- Developers working on custom Odoo implementations where test coverage is limited or inconsistent
- Technical leads looking for scalable ways to standardize testing across multiple clients
- Teams interested in applying AI not as a gimmick, but as a structured tool integrated into real development workflows

GKW Consult GmbH, a Germany-based engineering and consulting firm, was running on a fragmented legacy ERP system that could no longer keep pace with their project-driven business model. DirectPaie – Et si la paie française devenait enfin un atout dans Odoo ?
Description détaillée
---------------------
La paie française fait peur. Complexe, risquée, chronophage.
Résultat : dans la majorité des projets Odoo, elle reste externalisée, mal intégrée… ou évitée.
Et si c’était une erreur stratégique ?
Dans cette conférence, nous allons challenger cette idée reçue et montrer comment reprendre le contrôle de la paie, sans complexifier vos projets.
Avec DirectPaie, nous avons conçu un moteur de paie pensé dès le départ pour la France et pour Odoo :

- connecté à Odoo

L’objectif est simple : faire passer la paie de problème à éviter... à opportunité à saisir !

- La paie n’est plus un sujet à contourner dans Odoo

- Les intégrateurs peuvent reprendre la main sans devenir experts paie

Valeur apportée au public

- Des clés pour intégrer la paie dans vos projets sans augmenter le risque
- Un nouveau modèle de revenus récurrents à forte valeur
- Une meilleure maîtrise d’un sujet souvent subi

tracks.title: Stop Building Connectors: A Configuration-Driven Integration Framework for Odoo
tracks.speaker: Sebastien Didelot
tracks.speaker_raw: Sebastien Didelot, CEO at akolio
tracks.speaker_bio: Sébastien Didelot is the founder of Axup Business Solutions (axup.business => akol.io), where he designs and operates a multi-tenant, Kubernetes-hosted Odoo platform for SMEs and integration partners. Combining functional consulting with software architecture, he created Mosaic Tools — a configuration-driven integration framework that connects Odoo to external systems without bespoke code. He has delivered Odoo projects across retail, distribution, e-commerce and biomethane logistics, with a focus on integration patterns that scale across many instances and stay resilient through Odoo version upgrades.
tracks.description:
Every Odoo integrator knows the pattern: a new marketplace, a new carrier, a new platform — and yet another bespoke connector to build, test, and maintain. Multiply that across clients and Odoo versions, and integration becomes the single largest source of technical debt and migration pain in an ERP project.
This session presents a different approach: a universal, configuration-driven integration layer, native to Odoo. Instead of one Python module per external system, a multi-protocol API engine (REST, JSON-RPC, SOAP and GraphQL, with Basic / token / OAuth 2.0 authentication), a declarative connector (external system → resources → actions) and a mapping tool let you connect a new source by configuring it — not by launching a development project. When you hit a gap, you extend the framework once and every future integration benefits.
We show this live: connecting a real GraphQL API end-to-end — connection, request body, pagination, and field mapping — in minutes, without writing a new module. Then we share what running this in production teaches you, on a multi-tenant, Kubernetes-hosted Odoo platform where integrations must scale across dozens of instances and survive version upgrades.
Key takeaways: why one-off connectors don't scale and their hidden migration cost; how a config-driven, multi-protocol integration layer works in practice; a no-code example connecting an external API; and production lessons from a multi-tenant Odoo deployment.
Value for the audience: a reusable architectural pattern — not a product — that cuts integration time, lowers long-term maintenance, and stays resilient across Odoo upgrades.
Target audience: Odoo partners, integrators, technical consultants and developers, and functional decision-makers in retail, e-commerce and distribution who manage multiple sales channels and logistics providers.

tracks.description:
Norm is a Belgian manufacturer of custom kitchen and bathroom furniture that implemented Odoo as its central ERP, with a bidirectional integration with Ardis — their CNC cutting optimization software — as a hard requirement for go-live. From Odoo, confirmed manufacturing orders are written to a SQL database on Norm's internal network, where Ardis picks them up, groups them into production batches, and optimizes the cutting plans. The main technical challenges were unit conversion from mm² to m², barcode matching (Ardis uses a "W" prefix that had to be stripped), decoupling the production batch number from the MO status update, and the decision to exclude remainder plates from automatic stock deduction. Norm went live on 24 November 2025, seven months after kick-off, with a smooth go-live.

tracks.title: Escaping the Inventory Freeze: Just-in-Time Procurement in Odoo Enterprise
tracks.speaker: Tânia Manco
tracks.speaker_raw: Tânia Manco, ERP Consultant at much. Consulting
tracks.speaker_bio: Tânia Manco is a Consultant at much. Consulting, specializing in Odoo implementations for the commerce sectors across the DACH region. With a deep understanding of the Odoo stack, Tânia excels at bridging the gap between complex business requirements and scalable technical architecture.
tracks.description:
Why does stock sit dead on warehouse shelves? In standard Odoo, procurement counts forward. When a customer places an order for a future date, the system looks at the vendor lead time and triggers a purchase order immediately. If a supplier takes five days to deliver an item needed in a month, Odoo buys it now. The goods arrive weeks too early, locking up cash and taking up warehouse space. Meanwhile, standard reservation rules block that stock, preventing other active orders from using it.
To prevent such an inventory freeze, especially for high-volume warehouses, we built a backward-scheduling engine for Odoo Enterprise.
Instead of counting forward from the purchase date, the engine starts at the customer’s requested delivery date and counts backward. It determines the exact day to place the purchase order and the precise window to reserve warehouse stock. To match real-world supply chains, the calculation uses only weekdays (Monday to Friday).
The engine also isolates buying requirements for special project agreements from routine warehouse restocking, ensuring contract pricing applies correctly. When vendor lead times change, Odoo automatically updates open purchase orders and internal warehouse transfers. This automation keeps stock moving, frees up working capital, and cuts out manual scheduling work for procurement teams.
Key Points of This Talk:
- Optimising Odoo standard stock reservations with an automatically calculated backward-scheduled reservation window.
- Calculating purchasing deadlines backward from the sales delivery date using only weekdays.
- Separating specific project agreement purchases from standard restocking to maintain correct pricing.
- Automatically recalculating warehouse transfers and open orders when vendor lead times change.
Key Learnings:
- How to use Just-In-Time reservation windows to keep inventory available longer and free up capital.
- How to set up backward scheduling to tell your purchasing team exactly when to order based on customer requests.
- How to keep project-specific supply chains separate to protect special vendor pricing.
- How to handle vendor delays by having the system automatically adjust warehouse schedules.
Target Audience:
- Warehouse Managers and Operations Directors handling complex supply chains in Odoo
- Procurement Specialists managing complex vendor agreements
- Odoo Consultants and Architects looking for maintainable customization strategies

tracks.title: Multi-Agent Swarms for High-Performance ERP Migration in Odoo
tracks.speaker: Serena Palazzo
tracks.speaker_raw: Serena Palazzo, AI Team Leader at Rapsodoo
tracks.speaker_bio: Serena Palazzo is a delivery lead and data specialist at Symphonie Partners, focusing on Odoo implementations, system integrations, and data migrations. She has also worked on AI-driven projects, applying machine learning concepts to automate business processes. Serena designs and supports ETL pipelines using Python, PostgreSQL, and Google Cloud Platform. With a practical and structured approach, she helps connect business requirements with technical solutions to enable smooth and reliable ERP delivery.
tracks.description:
Enterprise ERP migrations toward Odoo are increasingly constrained by transformation complexity, heterogeneous schemas, and the need for near-zero downtime execution.
In this talk, we introduce a multi-agent swarm architecture designed to accelerate and parallelize data migration workflows through autonomous specialization and distributed decision-making. The system decomposes migration tasks into atomic responsibilities handled by coordinated AI agents, including schema decomposition agents, mapping inference agents, validation swarms, and conflict resolution agents.
We present a coordination layer inspired by swarm intelligence principles, where agents dynamically negotiate transformation strategies based on confidence scoring, constraint satisfaction signals, and historical migration performance metrics. This enables parallel exploration of multiple migration strategies while converging on optimal transformation paths.
The framework—internally referred to as the “AI Migration Syndicate”—is implemented on top of cloud-native execution environments with event-driven orchestration, allowing scalable execution of migration tasks across distributed workers. Special focus is given to deterministic fallback mechanisms, auditability, and reconciliation guarantees required in enterprise ERP contexts.
We conclude with real-world benchmarks demonstrating significant improvements in migration throughput, reduced manual intervention, and improved consistency in large-scale migrations into Odoo.

tracks.title: When Your Odoo Database Explodes: Understanding PG TOAST and How We Reduced 500GB to 60GB
tracks.speaker: Cristhian Ampudia
tracks.speaker_raw: Cristhian Ampudia, Asistente de Infraestructura at TRESCLOUD
tracks.speaker_bio: Cristhian Ampudia is an Odoo consultant and technical specialist at Trescloud, focused on performance optimization and scalable ERP architectures. He has extensive experience diagnosing and resolving complex issues in large Odoo deployments, including database optimization, integrations, and infrastructure tuning. Cristhian has helped multiple companies significantly reduce system costs and improve performance through deep technical analysis and practical solutions.
tracks.description:
As Odoo databases grow, hidden inefficiencies can silently increase storage usage and severely impact performance. One of the most overlooked causes is PostgreSQL TOAST (The Oversized-Attribute Storage Technique), especially when large binary data—such as base64-encoded images—is improperly stored in database fields.
In this talk, we present a real-world case where a client's Odoo database grew to over 500GB due to excessive storage of base64 images inside PostgreSQL tables. This led to performance degradation, slow backups, and increased infrastructure costs.
We will explain how TOAST works in PostgreSQL, how it affects Odoo installations, and how to identify when your database is suffering from TOAST-related bloat. We will also walk through the diagnostic process, including SQL queries and tools used to analyze table size, TOAST usage, and data patterns.
Most importantly, we will demonstrate the solution that reduced the database size from 500GB to 60GB, including data cleanup strategies, architectural improvements, and best practices to prevent this issue in future implementations.
Attendees will leave with practical techniques to audit their own databases, optimize storage, and significantly improve Odoo performance.
This session is ideal for Odoo developers, DevOps engineers, and technical consultants managing large-scale Odoo deployments.

He has a proven track record of re-architecting complex product and master-data frameworks within the retail sector, where he digitalized inventory workflows and built synchronized workflows across ERP, POS, and e-commerce channels.
tracks.description:
In high-volume dropshipping, a bloated IT infrastructure is the silent killer of scaling - and margins.
Managing hundreds of thousands of products across a fragmented software landscape disrupts vendor relationships and leaves businesses unable to react to rapid market price shifts.
This talk explores how we resolved this issue by consolidating operations, transforming Odoo 19 Enterprise into a "One-Stop" hub that harmonizes a large Shopware frontend with a lean, automated backend.
We will walk you through the journey of building a robust, step-based synchronization framework capable of handling extreme variant complexity - exceeding 400 options per product - while enabling real-time dropshipping automation.
From centralizing the product master to executing bulk vendor price updates across a quarter-million SKUs, this talk demonstrates how to scale a large catalog.
Key Points of this Talk:
- Infrastructure challenges of managing 250,000 dropshipping SKUs
- Overcoming the variant bottleneck: functional setup for products with 400+ options
- Designing a step-based synchronization framework between Shopware and Odoo 19
- Automating backend procurement triggers directly from frontend retail sales
- Centralizing vendor data to execute rapid bulk price updates
- Technical choices for balancing extreme data volumes with long-term Odoo stability
Key Learnings:
- How to replace fragmented legacy IT software landscapes with a single Odoo Enterprise core
- Methods to transition the operational "Source of Truth" in complex, multi-variant retail environments
- Strategies to architect automated dropshipping pipelines that eliminate manual intervention
- How to manage large-scale vendor data updates without causing database performance drops
- Project insights on balancing immediate business logic requirements with ERP maintainability
Target Audience:

tracks.title: Stop Answering the Same Tickets: Building a Self-Teaching Helpdesk with AI in Odoo 19
tracks.speaker: Mike Schulz
tracks.speaker_role: Senior Expert ERP Consulting at much. Consulting
tracks.speaker_raw: Mike Schulz, Senior Expert ERP Consulting at much. Consulting
tracks.speaker_bio: Mike Schulz is a Senior Expert ERP Consultant at much. Consulting, an Odoo Gold Partner, with offices in Germany, Portugal, and the UK. He helps companies of all sizes to drive growth and improve business processes with innovative Odoo Solutions. Mike is an expert in process automation and digital strategy, having successfully implemented countless Odoo projects to streamline operations and enhance efficiency.
tracks.description:
Service companies lose thousands of hours when their support teams are trapped answering the same Level-1 questions every single day. Without an automated system to record and share answers, agents constantly retype known solutions, which causes massive ticket backlogs and outdated knowledge bases.
To fix this structural bottleneck, we built a low-code, self-teaching loop completely inside the Odoo Enterprise v19 user interface.
We put a pipeline together by configuring three distinct native AI agents, linked with simple Automated Actions and basic Python UI snippets: an “initial responder” utilizing RAG, to answer clients using approved data, an “auditor” to check how tickets were closed, and a “writer” drafting new Knowledge Base articles By plugging in your own OpenAI or Gemini key directly into the frontend, this setup completely skips the need to build or maintain complex custom code modules. This working model proves that businesses can automatically turn daily ticket answers into permanent company documentation, cutting down future support volume and making advanced AI setups a practical reality.
Key Points of this Talk:
- Automating the Hand-Off: Configure Odoo Enterprise Helpdesk to trigger native ai.agents via Automated Actions.
- Forcing Factual Answers: Deploy native RAG parameters to restrict AI responses to approved Knowledge Base data.
- Skipping Custom Code: Evaluate how agents solved tickets using basic frontend Python snippets without custom module development.
- Self-Writing Documentation: Chain AI agents to automatically draft Odoo v19 Knowledge articles from closed tickets.
- Staying in the UI: Build this entire self-improving AI loop without ever leaving the native Odoo frontend.
Key Learnings:
- How to turn complex AI concepts into accessible, low-code Odoo v19 workflows.
- How to launch native AI agents using Automated Actions and simple screen logic.
- How to automatically turn human-resolved tickets into standard Knowledge Base articles.
- How to build a self-improving support system without heavy developer resources.
- How to set strict RAG boundaries to maintain data accuracy and prevent hallucinations.
Target Audience:
Business Leaders, Executives, and Functional Consultants using Odoo Enterprise v19+

tracks.title: The Two Hats of Odoo Python: Powering Core Logic vs. Driving User Experience
tracks.speaker: Gary Dolorfino
tracks.speaker_raw: Gary Dolorfino, Engineering Expert at much. Consulting
tracks.speaker_bio: Gary Dolorfino is an Odoo Expert at much. Consulting. In his role, he advises on complex ERP implementations, conducting system evaluations and audits that shape how clients get the most out of Odoo.
tracks.description:
This talk differentiates "Client-Facing Python" (UI events, dynamic views, computed fields) from "Core Backend Python" (business rules, data integrity, scheduled tasks, wizards) in Odoo development. Understanding this separation is crucial for building responsive, maintainable, and robust applications. The session will provide a framework for structuring Python code, optimizing performance and being intentional about UX implementation.
Key Points:
- Defining "Client-Facing" Python: onchange methods, button actions, dynamic UI Python (e.g., domains, field attributes), and UI-reflected computed fields.
- Defining "Core Backend" Python: ORM overrides (create(), write(), unlink()), scheduled actions, server actions, and complex wizard/data processing logic.
- Interaction & Data Flow: Examining how client-facing Python often acts as a gateway or pre/post-processor for core backend logic, and the pivotal role of the ORM as the bridge.
- Architectural Patterns & Best Practices: Strategies for keeping client-facing Python lean and responsive, isolating heavy logic in core backend Python (including considerations for asynchronous processing where applicable), ensuring security through input validation, and enhancing the testability of both code types.
- Practical Case Studies: Illustrating concepts with real-world examples, such as refactoring a performance-degrading onchange method and designing a button action that orchestrates multiple backend operations efficiently.
- Optimizing for Responsiveness: Actionable techniques to ensure client-facing Python supports, rather than hinders, a fluid and fast user interface.
Key Learnings:
- Attendees will be able to architect Odoo modules by clearly distinguishing the roles of their server-side Python code, separating UI-centric logic from core business operations.
- Attendees will learn to implement strategies to optimize Python code for responsive user interfaces, identifying and mitigating common performance bottlenecks associated with client-facing scripts.
- Attendees will understand how to design robust and efficient interactions and data flows between client-facing and core backend Python layers.
- Attendees will take away best practices for security (especially input validation from UI interactions) and testability tailored to the distinct characteristics of each type of Python code.
- Attendees will be equipped to refactor existing Odoo customizations for improved performance, maintainability, and scalability by applying these architectural principles.
Target Audience:
- Odoo Python Developers (Beginner and Intermediate)
- Odoo Technical Architects
- Technical Consultants involved in designing and implementing Odoo customizations
- Software Engineers working with the Odoo framework

tracks.title: The Art of Rapid Strategy Creation: Key to Business Success in Uncertain Times
tracks.speaker: Lars Sudman

tracks.title: How a €30M+ Supplement Manufacturer Is Moving from Legacy Tools to Odoo
tracks.speaker: Ferry Kluger
tracks.speaker_raw: Ferry Kluger, Founder at bobco GmbH
tracks.speaker_bio: Ferry is the founder and managing director of bobco GmbH, a Berlin-based ERP agency specializing in Odoo implementations for operationally complex and high-growth companies. Ferry's work focuses on turning messy real-world operations into clean, maintainable Odoo workflows.
tracks.description:
TISSO is a German nutritional supplement company founded in 1999. More than 20 years later, the company has grown into a €30M+ business with 159 employees and a complex operating model across own-brand B2C sales, subscriptions, B2B therapist and export business, and contract manufacturing.
From the outside, this looks like a modern supplement brand and manufacturer. Behind the scenes, the operational reality was more fragmented: Magento for eCommerce, bespoke ERP as a legacy order backbone, DATEV for accounting execution, Wrike and Google Sheets for coordination, and many manual handoffs between teams.
TISSO did not need “another tool.” It needed a real operating backbone.
In this session, TISSO and bob will share how the company approached Odoo as a phased business transformation: first stabilizing the commercial and finance backbone, then expanding toward Shopify, therapist portal improvements, procurement, inventory, and production.
The key decision was not to force a risky big-bang transformation. Instead, the first live scope focused on the narrowest slice that could create measurable business value: Order-to-Cash, subscriptions, therapist logic, fulfillment execution, invoicing, accounting operations, and reconciliation. This allowed the team to deprecate major legacy anchors while avoiding unnecessary go-live risk around full inventory, production, and valuation.
The long-term vision is broader: Odoo as the central system connecting multi-channel sales, finance, procurement, inventory, and production. But the implementation strategy was deliberately disciplined: prove the backbone first, simplify where possible, challenge unnecessary customizations, and only expand once the business has a stable operational baseline.
This talk is for companies and Odoo partners dealing with real mid-market complexity: legacy systems, partial previous implementations, custom code, multiple revenue streams, manufacturing requirements, finance dependencies, and teams that still rely heavily on spreadsheets and key-person knowledge.
What you’ll learn:
- How to scope an Odoo transformation for a mature company without creating big-bang go-live risk.
- Why the first ERP phase should focus on operational backbone, not maximum system replacement.
- How to decide what belongs in V1 and what must be delayed, even when the long-term ambition is much bigger.
- How TISSO approached Order-to-Cash, subscriptions, therapist business logic, fulfillment, finance handoffs, and reconciliation in Odoo.
- Why inventory, production, and procurement often need to be phased carefully rather than forced into the first go-live.
- How to use Odoo as the foundation for future transformation: Shopify migration, Odoo 19 upgrade, therapist portal expansion, inventory rollout, procurement, and production light.
- How customer and partner teams can work together during discovery, scope design, cutover, go-live, and hypercare.
- What other growing manufacturers can learn from TISSO’s journey from fragmented tools to one operating backbone.
<div

tracks.title: Scaling Support Excellence: Managing 100+ Daily Tickets Across Multiple Helpdesk Teams at GCU with Odoo
tracks.speaker: Anas Ouasmi
tracks.speaker_raw: Anas Ouasmi, Business Analyst at Sodexis
tracks.speaker_bio: Anas Ouasmi is a Business Analyst at Sodexis with 4 years of hands-on Odoo experience. tracks.description:
Are you struggling to keep up with an ever-increasing volume of customer support requests? Do tickets get lost in transit, or delayed due to manual routing inefficiencies across different internal departments? Managing multi-tier or departmental service desks presents a classic operational challenge: maintaining rapid response times without compromising service quality.
Enter GCU's modern support infrastructure! By leveraging Odoo Helpdesk, GCU transformed its support ecosystem to efficiently handle a heavy load of more than 100 tickets daily. This digital transformation replaced disjointed communication channels with a single, cohesive ticketing framework tailored for diverse operational and technical helpdesk teams.
With an intelligent automation layer, incoming inquiries are dynamically classified and assigned to specialized teams according to expertise, priority, and SLA metrics. Over the past year, this system has allowed GCU to process thousands of incoming issues, dramatically reducing resolution times and boosting user satisfaction across the organization. Service managers now gain real-time visibility through comprehensive analytical dashboards that track team performance and ticket bottlenecks.
Join this session to discover how GCU mapped its complex multi-team workflows to Odoo's native architecture, engineered robust automated workflows, and successfully scaled its operations to ensure a smooth, sustainable support journey.

tracks.title: Streamlining Sustainability: A Step-by-Step Guide to Odoo's ESG Configuration and Environmental Reporting
tracks.speaker: Vincent Allport
tracks.speaker_raw: Vincent Allport, Business Analyst at Sodexis
tracks.speaker_bio: Vincent Allport is a business analyst at Sodexis. With eight years of experience in Odoo, both as a user and as a business analyst, he brings a unique perspective to his customers to ensure their satisfaction and successful implementation.
tracks.description:
As regulatory bodies worldwide tighten disclosure requirements, Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) reporting has shifted from a corporate social responsibility checkbox to a critical compliance necessity. However, aggregating fragmented data from supply chains, energy bills, manufacturing outputs, and corporate travel often leaves sustainability officers buried under manual spreadsheets. How can businesses establish a single source of truth for their sustainability metrics without adding immense administrative overhead?
This session offers a comprehensive guide to navigating Odoo's newly enhanced sustainability architecture. We will explore how to model your company's environmental footprint directly within your ERP ecosystem. By connecting Odoo's core modules such as Purchase, Fleet, Manufacturing, and Accounting with native carbon accounting engines, organizations can capture resource consumption metrics automatically at the point of transaction.
Attendees will learn how to configure emission factors, map energy consumption metrics (Scope 1, 2, and 3 emissions), and establish tracking parameters for waste management and sustainable sourcing. We will also address how to customize data input criteria using Odoo Studio to meet specific local or international frameworks (such as CSRD or GRI), optimize calculation templates, and build dynamic sustainability dashboards. This ensures management teams have real-time visibility into their carbon intensity and green targets.
Join this practical session to transform compliance data tracking from a reactive annual burden into a proactive, automated workflow built entirely inside Odoo.
<div

tracks.title: One Distillery's Problem Becomes an Industry's Platform
tracks.speaker: Sebastian Navarro
tracks.speaker_role: Growth Lead & Technical Associate at MasterDistiller
tracks.speaker_raw: Sebastian Navarro, Growth Lead & Technical Associate at MasterDistiller
tracks.speaker_bio: Sebastian Navarro has spent over seven years in the spirits industry and knows the challenges spirits businesses face. Now at MasterDistiller, he pairs that industry knowledge with a technical programming background - bringing together Odoo's breadth and MasterDistiller's industry depth to deliver impactful solutions.
tracks.description:
MasterDistiller began with a single distillery and a problem the market could not solve. When a young whisky distillery set out to grow, it faced the same two options as everyone else: a sea of disconnected spreadsheets and paper records, or bulky generic ERP software that did not understand a distillery business. This talk tells the story of what came next, how the answer came from an industry-specific system built on the Odoo platform, and where it is heading.
Whisky demands full traceability, accurate maturation costing, and a single source of truth connecting production to finance, sales and planning across decades. The MasterDistiller team will show how Odoo's breadth becomes the foundation for a solution this specific, and why a vertical built on an open platform serves the spirits industry better than any of the old alternatives. MasterDistiller now supports distilleries across the UK, US, Canada and Australia, and every feature built for one client becomes a capability all of them can use.
Looking towards the future, because the platform is open source, extendible and easy to connect into, MasterDistiller is continually developing, including plugging emerging technologies like AI into the system to solve real business problems. The team will share the framework behind this, what the company calls Intelligent Distilling, as the next step in its journey.
Attendees will leave with a clear, practical view of how Odoo partners use platform breadth combined with industry depth to generate real value for their clients.
<div

tracks.title: The Last Unfakeable Thing - What our failed virtual exhibition taught us about digitising the wrong half of the business

tracks.speaker_raw: Denis Delforge, CEO at Brussels Expo

Under his direction, the organization has focused on modernization, sustainability, and strengthening Brussels’ position as a key European event hub. Delforge has been involved in managing large-scale events and developing partnerships that attract global audiences. Overall, he is recognized for his strategic vision and role in enhancing the international profile of Brussels’ exhibition sector.
tracks.description:
In 2020, with 120,000 m² of exhibition halls standing empty, we decided to build our own virtual trade show platform. It crashed. Meanwhile, other platforms raised extraordinary valuations on the same premise and then the bubble deflated just as fast.
Five years on, physical gathering is thriving. Denis Delforge, CEO of Brussels Expo, argues the entire industry made the same mistake: we tried to digitise the experience, when what needed digitising was the relationship. Who actually comes through the door, why, and what happens next, a question venues have never been able to answer.
An honest account of a failure, a bubble, and what a 1935 building is doing about it now: white-label ticketing, on-site data, and why the most analogue business in the world is becoming a data business.
