tracks.title: From CAD to ERP: Creating a Single Source of Truth with SolidWorks, Onshape and Odoo
tracks.speaker: Eduardo Magdalena García
tracks.speaker_role: Founder & CEO at C2i Change 2 improve Optimización de procesos, S.L.
tracks.speaker_raw: Eduardo Magdalena García, Founder & CEO at C2i Change 2 improve Optimización de procesos, S.L.
tracks.speaker_bio: Eduardo Magdalena is a mechanical engineer and founder of C2i - Change 2 improve, an Odoo and Onshape partner specialized in process optimization and CAD-ERP integration. He holds a Master's Degree in ICT Business Management and has more than 25 years of experience helping engineering and manufacturing companies improve their processes through technology. Former Technical Director of a SolidWorks reseller in Spain, he currently develops integration solutions that connect CAD systems such as SolidWorks and Onshape with Odoo, creating a unified digital workflow across engineering, manufacturing and business operations.
tracks.description:
When information does not flow, companies lose time, money and competitiveness.
In many manufacturing companies, engineering teams create products, assemblies, bills of materials and technical documentation in CAD systems such as SolidWorks or Onshape. However, much of this information never reaches the ERP because manually transferring and maintaining it is too time-consuming and error-prone.
As designs evolve, data quickly becomes outdated, duplicated or inconsistent across departments. As a result, many companies are unable to fully leverage the capabilities of Odoo Manufacturing, Inventory, Purchasing, Projects and other business applications because critical product information is either incomplete or disconnected from the engineering source.
This session explores how a Single Source of Truth approach can bridge the gap between engineering and business operations. Based on real-world CAD-ERP integration projects currently used in manufacturing environments, attendees will discover how SolidWorks, Onshape and Odoo can work together to create a connected digital workflow where product data, bills of materials, design changes, documentation and images remain synchronized throughout the entire product lifecycle.
A live demonstration based on real customer implementations will show how engineering information can flow automatically from CAD into Odoo, reducing manual work, improving traceability and enabling more reliable decision-making across engineering, purchasing, manufacturing and inventory teams.
Attendees will learn:
• Why critical engineering information often never reaches the ERP.
• How disconnected systems create inefficiencies, errors and hidden costs.
• How a Single Source of Truth approach improves consistency, collaboration and traceability.
• How SolidWorks, Onshape and Odoo can work together in real manufacturing environments.
This session is intended for manufacturing companies, engineering teams, operations managers, Odoo partners and anyone interested in improving industrial processes through better information management and system integration.
<div

tracks.speaker_raw: Jochem Bauwmans and Cindy Singh, Project manager at Dynapps
tracks.speaker_bio: Jochem Bauwmans is Project manager at Dynapps, leading mid-size Odoo implementations in the Belgian and Dutch markets.

Our client installs solar panels, batteries, heat pumps and charging stations for B2C and B2B customers across Belgium. Before Odoo they ran on Teamleader for CRM, Simple-Simon for technician scheduling, AppSheet for on-site checklists, Google Drive for the customer file, SolarEdge for design and monitoring, and ClearFacts for accounting —  five disconnected tools with constant copy-paste between them and no single view of a deal, a job or a customer. In this session we show how Dynapps consolidated that entire stack into one Odoo platform covering the full lifecycle: lead capture across web/portal/socials, a three-pipeline CRM (B2B, particulier, EcoCare), commissioning models per salesperson, quote duplication and PDF templating, automated Google Drive folder creation per opportunity, a SolarEdge Designer deep-link directly on the lead, mobile-friendly site-visit and installation checklists with sketches, photos and conditional fields, employee scheduling and work-order e-signature for the field technician, inspection registration and single-line-diagram handover, helpdesk with SLAs and multiple teams, tickets auto-created from SolarEdge alerts, recurring EcoCare maintenance subscriptions with SEPA direct debit, and an accountant-friendly handover to ACS. tracks.title: Quality Control process
tracks.speaker: CRETU Victor
tracks.speaker_raw: CRETU Victor, Business Analyst at Sodexis SAS
tracks.speaker_bio: Victor CRETU est business analyste et travaille chez Sodexis depuis 2 ans. Il a une expérience de 6 ans à l'utilisation de Odoo. Il a accompagné beaucoup d'entreprises de différentes tailles dans leur implémentation de Odoo.
tracks.description:
For Amel, maintaining high product standards while keeping warehouse operations efficient is a top priority. However, manual tracking of arriving shipments and disconnected quality check processes were creating bottlenecks.
By implementing a tailored Quality Control and Inventory solution using Odoo, Amel transformed its inbound logistics. The new system automatically alerts operators when products arrive and intelligently routes specific items through a rigorous quality check process, saving valuable time and drastically reducing manual errors.
The Challenge: Bottlenecks in the Receiving Process
Before the Odoo implementation, Amel's warehouse team faced three primary operational hurdles:
1) Communication Gaps: Operators on the floor were not immediately aware when new shipments arrived at the loading dock, leading to delays in unloading, putaway, and processing.
2) Inconsistent Quality Routing: Identifying which incoming products required a quality inspection was a manual, error-prone process. This occasionally led to items bypassing quality checks and moving directly into available stock.
3) Wasted Time: Warehouse staff spent excessive time physically tracking down paperwork, communicating arrivals via radio or in-person, and manually updating spreadsheets to coordinate quality control tasks.
The Odoo Solution
To solve these challenges, Amel utilized a combination of Odoo's Inventory, Quality, and Discuss/Automation applications. The solution was designed to create a seamless, automated flow from the moment a truck arrives to the moment a product hits the shelves.
1. Real-Time Operator Notifications
To solve the communication gap, Odoo was configured to act as the central nervous system for the warehouse floor.
- Automated Chatter & Discuss Alerts: Whenever a shipment is scanned and marked as "Received" in the Odoo Inventory app, an automated action instantly pings the designated warehouse channel in Odoo Discuss.
- Complete Visibility: All operators receive a real-time notification on their devices (tablets or workstations) detailing the receipt number, the supplier, and the items that have just arrived. Everyone is instantly on the same page, eliminating idle time.
2. Smart Quality Control Routing
Instead of relying on human memory or paper checklists to decide what needs testing, Amel leveraged Odoo's Quality Control Points (QCP).
- Targeted Inspections: Quality Control Points were configured for specific products, product categories, or specific vendors that have historically required closer monitoring.
- Automated Intervention: When a receipt containing these specific products is processed, Odoo automatically generates a "Quality Check" task. The inventory move is effectively paused; the system prevents the products from being moved into general stock until the Quality team logs in, performs the required checks (e.g., measuring dimensions, taking photos, or simple Pass/Fail tests), and validates the operation.
Key Benefits and Results
The integration of Odoo's Inventory and Quality modules delivered immediate, measurable impact for Amel:
- Massive Time Savings: By eliminating manual data entry, paper trails, and unnecessary communication delays, the warehouse team reallocated their time toward processing shipments faster.
- Zero-Defect Receiving: Because Odoo physically restricts the movement of flagged items until a Quality Check is passed, the risk of defective products entering the supply chain has been completely neutralized.
- Empowered Operators: Warehouse staff no longer have to guess or ask around about incoming shipments. The automated notification system ensures complete transparency, allowing operators to prioritize their tasks dynamically based on real-time arrivals.
Conclusion
By standardizing its receiving and quality control processes within Odoo, Amel has achieved a highly transparent, efficient, and reliable inbound supply chain. The solution guarantees that operators are always informed and that every critical product is thoroughly vetted before it ever reaches the shelves—safeguarding Amel's reputation for quality without sacrificing speed.

tracks.title: How to unify and scale multi-channel business operations at a 50m+ E-Commerce brand
tracks.speaker: Ferry Kluger
tracks.speaker_raw: Ferry Kluger, Co-founder at bobco GmbH
tracks.speaker_bio: Ferry is the founder and managing director of bobco GmbH, a Berlin-based ERP agency specializing in Odoo implementations for operationally complex and high-growth companies. In this session, Ferry will co-present with Rosental, sharing how a fast-growing eCommerce brand approached Odoo not as a full replatforming project, but as the foundation for scalable operations, clean data, better financial control, and a stronger B2B business.
tracks.description:
Fast-growing eCommerce companies often look very modern from the outside. Strong brand, high order volume, advanced marketing, automated fulfillment, and a polished customer experience.
But behind the scenes, the operational backbone often tells a different story: product master data in several sheets, supply chain planning in spreadsheets, purchasing outside the ERP, inventory valuation patched manually, B2B sales managed through inboxes, and finance teams trying to reconcile numbers that were never generated from one coherent process.
That was the starting point for Rosental. The obvious mistake would have been to “replace everything” in one giant ERP project. That is how many ERP implementations drag on forever, lose focus, and create unnecessary operational risk.
Instead, we used a stricter playbook: protect what already works, identify where the business urgently needs a single source of truth, and implement Odoo first where it creates the highest operational leverage.
In this talk, Rosental and bob will walk through the Odoo implementation strategy from A to Z: discovery, pain quantification, scope design, phased rollout, master data cleanup, procurement, inventory valuation, B2B order-to-cash, fulfillment integration, financial control, and post-go-live improvement.
The main lesson: for high-growth eCommerce brands, Odoo does not need to replace the entire commerce stack on day one. It needs to become the operational backbone that connects product data, purchasing, inventory, valuation, B2B sales, and finance.
What you’ll learn:
- How to scope an Odoo implementation for a high-growth eCommerce company without creating unnecessary go-live risk.
- Why the first ERP phase should focus on operational truth, not maximum system replacement.
- How to identify the “hero work” that signals broken processes and fragmented data.
- How to decide what belongs in Odoo first: master data, purchasing, inventory, valuation, B2B sales, finance, and integrations.
- How to phase an implementation so the business gets value quickly while leaving room for continuous improvement.
- Why clean product and supplier data is the foundation for COGS, inventory valuation, supply chain visibility, and finance.
- How customer and partner teams can work together during discovery, migration, go-live, and stabilization.

Serkan Özcan is a Principal Project Leader & Consultant at braintec with over seven years of experience implementing Odoo ERP. With a degree in Business Information Technology and a background in IT audit and business analysis at PwC, Serkan brings a structured, risk-aware view of business processes to every project.
He has led dozens of implementations for companies of nearly every size, from one-person businesses to international groups, across trade, events and professional services. That range taught him how much Odoo's standard already covers, and that the craft lies in fitting it precisely to the business.
tracks.description:
Moving beyond standard bookkeeping, large-scale corporate portfolios require a level of financial orchestration that often seems at odds with "out-of-the-box" ERP logic. This session presents a success story of a major group implementation—initially pitched against SAP/Haufe—where a full functional go-live was achieved in just two months. The challenge? A centralized "In-House Bank" model where subsidiaries operate without independent cash outflows, requiring complex transversal settlements and automated month-end netting.
The core value of this talk lies in demonstrating that Odoo’s framework is powerful enough to handle non-standard accounting processes, provided one possesses a deep architectural understanding of its engine. We will explore how a "Standard-First" philosophy, supplemented by surgical SQL-based data extraction and lightweight core extensions, can solve even the most rigid corporate requirements.
Key Learnings for the Audience:
The "Engine-First" Approach: Why deep framework knowledge is the prerequisite for solving complex, non-standard accounting workflows through configuration.
Transversal Settlement Architecture: A technical breakdown of how to manage a "Parent-as-Bank" model, using Odoo’s internal mechanisms to bridge subsidiary payables and parent cash.
Surgical Data Extraction: How to use targeted SQL queries to pull high-performance reporting data out of Odoo when standard UI views reach their limits.
Balancing Core & Custom: Identifying the thin line between "good configuration" and "necessary extension" to keep the system upgradeable and audit-ready.
Value for the Audience:
Attendees will see a transparent look at a high-level integration that goes beyond basic tutorials. You will learn how to architect Odoo for a multi-entity portfolio by leaning on its native strengths while using expert-level technical maneuvers (SQL and slight core adaptations) to fill the gaps. This talk serves as a blueprint for consultants and CFOs who need to deliver enterprise-grade financial results in record time.
Target Audience:
Senior Functional Consultants, Odoo Architects, CFOs, and Financial Controllers who deal with multi-company environments and high-complexity accounting.

tracks.title: Opening a Café with Odoo: How Café Hoch³ Built a Digital Business Setup from Day One
tracks.speaker: David Goerke
tracks.speaker_raw: David Goerke, Managing Director at Café Hoch³
tracks.speaker_bio: David Goerke is Managing Director of Café Hoch³ in Stralsund and combines entrepreneurial hands-on execution with experience in digital transformation. Alongside his role in the café business, he is active in nonprofit leadership and business development. Earlier in his career, he also worked in software engineering and operational social-impact environments. For the opening of Café Hoch³, he chose a strongly digital operating model from day one and established Odoo as the central platform for key business processes.
tracks.description:
How can a newly opened café build a digital, integrated and pragmatic business setup from day one? This session presents the story of Café Hoch³ in Stralsund, where Odoo was introduced as the central business platform right from the opening. The café uses Odoo for point of sale, website, accounting, loyalty and discount programs, and WhatsApp-based customer communication. A particularly interesting aspect is that Managing Director David Goerke implemented most of the Odoo setup himself, while Intero supported him selectively with app selection, hardware-related questions and setup guidance. This makes the talk more than a standard implementation story. It becomes a practical example of enabled self-implementation: a model in which the customer takes ownership of large parts of the rollout while still benefiting from expert guidance where needed. It illustrates how Odoo can be an excellent fit for smaller and fast-moving hospitality businesses that value standardization, usability and speed of execution.
The session will cover how to choose the right Odoo apps for gastronomy, how to connect front-office and back-office processes in one system, and what matters when selecting a modern point-of-sale setup for café operations. The original story especially highlights Odoo’s intuitive interface, modular scalability, mobile usability and seamless integration across apps. Attendees will gain practical insights into launching a hospitality business with Odoo, structuring a digital operating model from the beginning, and balancing self-service implementation with targeted partner support.

tracks.title: The day Biometrics met real users: an Odoo case study
tracks.speaker: Elena Khodiachaya
tracks.speaker_role: Odoo Consultant & Business Analyst at Ventor Tech
tracks.speaker_raw: Elena Khodiachaya, Odoo Consultant & Business Analyst at Ventor Tech
tracks.speaker_bio: Elena Khodiachaya is an Odoo Consultant & Business Analyst at VentorTech with a strong background in quality assurance and business process analysis. Her QA experience helps her approach Odoo implementations with a focus on system reliability, clear requirements, and well-tested workflows. She works closely with clients to translate business needs into practical Odoo solutions, with particular attention to process optimization, usability, and implementation quality. Elena turns complexity into clarity and makes difficult things easy to understand.
tracks.description:
This is a real Odoo case showing how to make biometric attendance resilient to real-world user behavior.
The client deployed biometric attendance expecting accurate and fully automated time tracking. In practice, everyday user behavior exposed process gaps that resulted in attendance inconsistencies, payroll issues, and manual corrections.
KEY LEARNINGS
- Biometric identification alone does not guarantee accurate attendance
- Common user workarounds: incorrect punch types, forgotten check-outs, badge sharing, and mixed entry/exit points
- Inconsistent biometric events can be detected and classified automatically
- A single incorrect punch can trigger multiple attendance errors if not properly handled
- Guided correction workflows improve payroll accuracy while reducing HR effort
- Attendance and payroll can be safely reprocessed after schedule changes
VALUES FOR THE AUDIENCE
Practical techniques for making attendance processes in Odoo more reliable, reducing manual HR effort, and improving the quality of attendance data used for payroll and overtime control.
TARGET AUDIENCE
- Business Owners
- Manufacturing Managers
- Warehouse Managers
- HR Managers
- Payroll Specialists
- System Administrators
- Security Specialists
- Solution Architects

tracks.title: Building High-Performance Odoo eCommerce with S3 and Google Merchant Center.
tracks.speaker: Benjamin Seeßle
tracks.speaker_raw: Benjamin Seeßle, ERP Consultant at much. Consulting
tracks.speaker_bio: Benjamin Seeßle is an ERP Consultant at much. Consulting, specializing in digital transformation, master-data restructuring, and enterprise process design. He has a proven track record of re-architecting complex product and master-data frameworks within the retail sector, where he digitalized inventory workflows and built synchronized workflows across ERP, POS, and e-commerce channels.
tracks.description:
Launching an Odoo eCommerce site from scratch with a large catalog requires more than just a beautiful theme; it demands a "Performance-First" infrastructure, so your system doesn't slow down. This talk breaks down a real-world implementation strategy for businesses launching with over 1,000 SKUs and 500+ daily visitors, where technical scalability is the primary constraint. We move past the standard Odoo Website builder to show how offloading heavy media - such as high-resolution product videos and images - to AWS S3 and a Global CDN preserves Odoo worker capacity for critical backend tasks.
We will also tackle the tricky parts of multi-channel scaling by deep-diving into Google Merchant Center integration. You will learn how to resolve technical "mismatches" in Odoo’s standard product feeds, specifically focusing on how to map your categories and sync product attributes so Google doesn't penalize your indexing. Finally, we'll address the importance of project timeline to make sure your pricing and sales channels are fully planned out before any coding starts, bridging the gap between your marketing goals and technical reality in Odoo Enterprise.
Key Points of the Talk:
- Speed Optimization: Offloading media rendering to S3/CDN to keep workers free so Odoo runs faster.
- Better Product Feeds: Matching Odoo product variants to Google Merchant Center’s rigid categories.
- Infrastructure Scaffolding: Setting up your technical foundation so it is ready for future product configurators and marketing automation.
- UX via Data: Using Odoo Product Tags and filters so customers can easily browse large catalogs.
- Global Latency: Using CDNs to ensure the site loads quickly for shoppers anywhere in the world.
- Timeline Alignment: Managing implementation milestones to ensure data-ready "Day One" launches.
Key Learnings:
- How to offload heavy website files to external clouds so your Odoo’s performance doesn't degrade.
- How to reconcile Odoo’s flexible product categories with Google’s mandatory taxonomy for Merchant Center.
- How to avoid common SEO/Google penalties caused by poor-quality product feed data.
- How to build a flexible B2C/B2B theme that easily handles large catalogs using Odoo’s built-in filters.
Target Audience:
- Project Managers & Consultants overseeing complex eCommerce migrations.
- E-commerce Managers scaling catalogs beyond 1k SKUs on Odoo Enterprise.

This talk tells the story of how Zero, implemented and scaled Odoo to manage a resort where operational excellence isn't optional — it's the entire brand promise. When your guests include global icons who expect perfection, your back-office has zero room for error.

How we unified every operation under one Odoo instance — restaurants, bars, beach service, spa, marina, retail, conference facilities, and villa management — each with its own POS terminal posting to a centralized accounting ledger in real time. Target audience: Odoo partners looking to break into the hospitality and tourism vertical, resort and hotel operators evaluating Odoo as an alternative to legacy PMS/POS systems, and anyone interested in multi-venue, multi-company Odoo architectures for complex service businesses.

tracks.title: The ultimate guide to run your sport club on Odoo
tracks.speaker: Emile Gillieaux
tracks.speaker_raw: Emile Gillieaux, Account Manager at Odoo
tracks.description:
Managing a sports club in Odoo creates a seamless, automated workflow by connecting your website, membership management, bookings, and events into a single ecosystem. It all begins on your Odoo Website, where prospective members browse subscription plans, court availabilities, and upcoming events. When a user selects a membership and pays online, Odoo instantly creates their profile in the CRM, generates a recurring contract, and issues the first invoice. Behind the scenes, the Subscriptions module takes over the membership lifecycle, securely storing member data, tracking payment statuses, and automating future billings. For daily operations, members use the Appointments module on the website to book real-time slots for court rentals, choosing their preferred sport, terrain, and time. This booking tool syncs with the club's schedule to prevent double bookings, issues confirmation emails, and can process rental fees on the spot for non-members. Finally, larger activities like classes, tournaments, or high-stakes championship games are managed through the Events module, which automatically publishes them to the website. To handle premier matches with limited seating, you can define maximum capacity limits for the venue and configure multiple ticket tiers. This allows you to set tiered pricing based on the seats such as VIP courtside, premium stands, or standard general admission. Members register online, select their tier, and receive a confirmation email featuring a unique QR code. On game day, staff scan these codes at the gate via their phones to securely check participants in, validate seat categories, and instantly update the club's attendance and revenue records.

tracks.title: Multi-database synchronization: Technical challenges and design patterns
tracks.speaker: Stanislas Gueniffey
tracks.speaker_raw: Stanislas Gueniffey, Customisations Architect at Odoo
tracks.speaker_bio:
Hello? (Hello? Hello? Hello?)
Is there anybody in there?
Just nod if you can hear me
Is there anyone home?
tracks.description:
Multi-DB Synchronization: Technical Challenges and Design Patterns
Multi-database integrations offer massive functional value, but synchronizing complex data across independent systems is notoriously risky. When standard multi-company configurations are no longer viable, custom synchronization architectures become essential. In this technical talk, we will explore advanced design patterns for building robust, transport-agnostic synchronization engines. Attendees will learn how to safely resolve cross-database relational dependencies using idempotent payload ingestion and "heal-in-place" stub records. We will also tackle performance bottlenecks by designing an O(1) bulk data loader, leveraging 3-pass imports and deferred post-commits to prevent worker crashes during massive data syncs. Finally, we will cover modern strategies for exchanging large binary files without crippling database performance. This talk equips developers and architects with a concrete toolkit of design patterns to turn complex multi-database integrations into stable, predictable successes.
Disclaimer : The patterns discussed in this talk are not part of the Odoo standard nor any future roadmap. They represent generic architectural guidelines and best-practice design patterns for building synchronization engines

tracks.title: Why International Companies with a German Entity Don't Need DATEV — Audit-Ready Accounting in Odoo
tracks.speaker: Florian Pichl
tracks.speaker_raw: Florian Pichl, CFO at syscoon GmbH
tracks.description:
"If you operate in Germany, you need DATEV." For decades, international groups expanding into Germany have heard this from their local tax advisor — and accepted it as a fact. The result: a parallel German accounting silo, an interface to maintain, additional licenses, and a German entity that only becomes visible to headquarters at month-end.
This talk challenges that belief and shows why DATEV is no longer a requirement for most international companies running a German entity in Odoo.
We walk through, function by function, how Odoo covers the full scope of German accounting inside a multi-company, multi-currency group setup: GoBD-compliant bookkeeping, complete audit trails, SKR03/SKR04 charts of accounts, the German VAT statement (Umsatzsteuervoranmeldung), e-invoicing for Germany, and direct collaboration with external tax advisors — with a clean DATEV export available when it is genuinely needed.
The real value is integration. With Odoo, the German entity reports into the same system as the rest of the group: one chart of accounts mapping, one source of truth from sales order to consolidated P&L, no end-of-month import from a separate accounting island. That eliminates reconciliation work, double tooling, and interface costs — and gives headquarters real-time visibility into the German operation.
Attendees will leave with a clear framework for when DATEV is truly required, when it is not, and how to position Odoo confidently with international finance teams and their German tax advisors. The session is built for CFOs and Heads of Finance of international groups operating in Germany — and for Odoo partners serving them.

tracks.title: Odoo HR for 3,000 Plantation Workers: Attendance, Daily Wages, and Labor Law Compliance Across 12 Remote Sites
tracks.speaker: Akhmad Daniel Sembiring
tracks.speaker_raw: Akhmad Daniel Sembiring, CEO at Vitraining
tracks.speaker_bio:
Akhmad is the CEO and Founder of VITRAINING, an Indonesian technology consultancy with over two decades of enterprise ERP implementation experience. As an Odoo contributor since 2010, VITRAINING has delivered end-to-end Odoo implementations for more than 100 organizations across Indonesia, spanning state-owned enterprises (BUMN), agribusiness conglomerates, manufacturing companies, and government agencies.
His current focus areas include AI-augmented ERP workflows using DeepSeek and ChatGPT, custom Odoo frontend development with Apache ECharts and OWL framework, blockchain integration for supply chain traceability, and carbon credit verification platforms. He is a regular contributor to the Indonesian Odoo community and is passionate about bridging the gap between enterprise-grade ERP capabilities and the operational realities of businesses in Southeast Asia.
tracks.description:
How VITRAINING built a mobile-first Odoo HR system for a geographically dispersed plantation workforce in Riau, Kalimantan, and Jambi — where internet is spotty and labor regulations are strict.
Abstract
Managing HR for a large plantation workforce is fundamentally different from managing HR in an office environment. Workers are distributed across 12 remote sites spanning three Indonesian provinces. Internet connectivity is unreliable. Daily wage calculations depend on harvest output (Fresh Fruit Bunch kilograms per worker per day), not fixed salaries. And Indonesian labor law (UU Ketenagakerjaan) mandates specific overtime, religious holiday allowances, and BPJS Ketenagakerjaan social security contributions for every worker — even casual daily laborers.
In this talk, VITRAINING presents how we configured and extended Odoo 17 HR and Payroll modules to handle this exact scenario: a mobile-first attendance system using QR codes that syncs to Odoo in batch when connectivity is available; a dynamic daily wage calculation engine tied to actual harvest output recorded in the Inventory module; automated BPJS contribution calculations and government report generation; and a multi-site leave management system that respects 6 different regional public holiday calendars.
We will also cover how we handled the edge cases: workers who split time across multiple sites in a single day, harvest bonus pooling at the team level, and retroactive payroll corrections when harvest weight data is revised after mill processing.
This is a practical, field-tested HR configuration story with direct applicability for any Odoo partner working with plantation, mining, construction, or distributed workforce clients globally.
Key Takeaways for Attendees
● Offline-capable QR attendance system architecture that batch-syncs to Odoo HR when connectivity is restored
● Output-based daily wage calculation: linking Odoo Inventory (harvest kg) to Payroll computation rules
● Indonesian BPJS Ketenagakerjaan and BPJS Kesehatan automated contribution calculation and reporting
● Multi-site, multi-calendar leave management across 12 locations with different regional holidays
● Retroactive payroll correction workflow for plantation harvest weight revisions post mill-processing
Target Audience
HR managers, Odoo payroll consultants, partners serving agriculture/plantation/mining/construction verticals, distributed workforce operations
Odoo Modules Featured
HR, Payroll, Attendance, Leave Management, Inventory (harvest integration), custom BPJS module

tracks.speaker: Bright Obeng
tracks.speaker_raw: Bright Obeng, Managing Director at CFO Studios
tracks.speaker_bio: Bright Obeng is an entrepreneur, founder of CFO Studios and host of De CFO Podcast, one of Belgium’s leading platforms for CFOs and finance leaders.
tracks.description:
Finance is often described as a function: reporting, budgeting, controlling, compliance, risk and cash management.
All of that remains essential. But it is no longer enough.
In this keynote, Bright Obeng introduces the central idea behind his upcoming book: the modern CFO should not be understood merely as the owner of numbers, but as a critical force in the quality of decisions an organisation makes.
The embedded CFO is close enough to the business to understand where value is created, where it leaks away and where decisions really take shape. But at the same time, the embedded CFO remains independent enough to challenge assumptions, expose trade-offs and protect the organisation from decisions that look attractive on paper but destroy value in practice.
Bright explores why finance must move beyond reporting what happened and become more actively involved in how decisions are sensed, framed, chosen, committed to and protected. In that sense, finance is not just a function. It is a decision-making capability.
This keynote is a sharp and practical reflection on the future of finance, the changing role of the CFO and the importance of embedding finance deeper into the business without losing its independence. It invites leaders to rethink one fundamental question: is finance in your organisation mainly producing reports, or is it helping the business make better decisions?
The keynote is linked to Bright's upcoming book, the first CFO book written in Belgium (for now, in the Dutch version). This book will be launched in November 2026.

tracks.description:
Manufacturing companies generate a large amount of information throughout a product's lifecycle, but this data is often scattered across different Odoo modules. Understanding the complete history of a product frequently requires navigating through multiple menus and documents.
In this talk, we will introduce the Digital History Record (DHR), a unified product view that aggregates manufacturing, quality controls, purchases, sales, support tickets, inventory movements, lots, and related documentation into a single interface.
We will explain how the DHR has been designed to leverage existing Odoo data without duplicating information, providing users with immediate access to the complete lifecycle of every product.

tracks.title: Odoo vs. Oracle Opera: Why One of Albania's Top Resorts Chose Odoo to Run Its Entire Hotel Operation
tracks.speaker: Arnold Kadiu
tracks.speaker_role: Ceo at Zero l Odoo Partner
tracks.speaker_raw: Arnold Kadiu, Ceo at Zero l Odoo Partner
tracks.speaker_bio: Arnold Kadiu is the CEO and founder of Zero Group, one of the first Odoo Partners in the Balkans and an Odoo Gold Partner since 2022. He has led Odoo implementations across hospitality, banking, manufacturing, real estate, and e-governance for clients in Albania, Kosovo, Malta. Zero has expanded its hospitality solution to cover channel management, IoT integrations, and multi-property operations, establishing Odoo as a viable all-in-one alternative to legacy hotel management systems.
tracks.description:
When Kaiser Resort — a luxury beachfront property on the Albanian Riviera — needed to digitize its hotel operations, they evaluated Oracle Opera, the global industry standard used by Hilton, Marriott, and Accor. They chose Odoo instead. This talk explains exactly why, and what happened next.
Oracle Opera is the undisputed king of hotel property management systems, powering over 40,000 hotels worldwide. Every hospitality CTO knows it. So when a resort operator looks at both platforms side by side and picks Odoo, the "why" matters — not just for this hotel, but for every Odoo partner considering whether to pursue the hospitality vertical.
What we'll cover:
The real evaluation criteria that drove Kaiser's decision. Oracle Opera is a powerful PMS — but it is a PMS only. It doesn't do accounting. It doesn't do purchasing. It doesn't do inventory. It doesn't manage your restaurant POS natively. For a resort that needs front desk, restaurant, beach bar, pool bar, housekeeping, procurement, and accounting to talk to each other in real time, Opera means buying five systems and hoping the integrations hold. Odoo means one login, one database, one truth.
We'll walk through how Kaiser Resort runs today on Odoo: reservations flowing into the front desk, guests checking in, POS charges from the beach bar and restaurant posting to guest folios, housekeeping tracked in real time, purchasing and inventory managing everything from linens to the kitchen, and every transaction ending in the accounting module — automatically, without reconciliation.
We'll share the channel manager integrations for connecting Kaiser to Booking.com and other OTAs, how reservations sync into Odoo in real time, and how cancellations are handled automatically.
Key learnings for the audience:
- A transparent, honest comparison of Odoo vs. Oracle Opera from the operator's perspective — where Odoo wins, where Opera has advantages, and why the "all-in-one" argument is the decisive factor for independent resorts.
- How to implement a full hotel operation on Odoo: PMS (reservations, check-in/out, folios), POS (restaurant, bar, beach), Purchasing, Inventory, and Accounting — working as one integrated system
- Channel Manager integration architecture: Real-time sync for reservations, availability, rates, and cancellations.
- The business case for Odoo in hospitality: what it costs vs. Oracle Opera, what the operator gains, and what Odoo partners should know before selling into this vertical
Target audience: Odoo partners evaluating the hospitality market, hotel and resort operators comparing Odoo to legacy PMS solutions like Oracle Opera or Protel, and anyone curious about what it takes to compete with enterprise hospitality software using Odoo.

tracks.speaker_raw: Frédéric Neus, CEO & Founder at Oxalyo
tracks.speaker_bio: Frédéric Neus is the CEO and Founder of OXALYO, an Odoo implementation and strategic advisory partner for industrial SMEs. He built his expertise over 25 years in senior financial and operational roles at Kodak (13 years, from accounting to business unit CFO) and Puratos (10 years, as CFO Europe, CFO & COO Brazil, and CFO Middle East). This hands-on international experience across complex, fast-changing environments shaped his conviction that SME leaders deserve the same financial clarity and operational structure as large corporations, which led him to found OXALYO.
tracks.description:
Gegolac is a family-run industrial company with over 30 years of expertise in aluminum surface treatment. After a bold €7 million investment in its production facilities, Mirko Morici, Managing Director of Gegolac, set out to bring the same level of ambition to the company's processes and management tools, starting with Odoo, which was already in place but only partially leveraged.
In this talk, Frédéric Neus, CEO of OXALYO, will share how his team partnered with Mirko and the Gegolac team to unlock the full potential of Odoo: restructuring internal processes, strengthening financial steering and transforming the ERP into a genuine management and decision-making tool.
The audience will discover how concrete improvements (automated sales flows, electronic delivery note signatures on tablet, better inventory management, tighter monthly closings, budgeting and forecasting, and real-time margin visibility) translated into measurable business results: +25% revenue growth, a €400,000 EBITDA improvement, and +50% growth in Q1 2026 vs. Q1 2025.
Beyond the numbers, this session will explore what it truly means to align ERP optimization with the operational reality of an industrial SME, and how a well-structured Odoo project can become a source of clarity and confidence for leadership.
This session is especially relevant for SME leaders, operations managers, CFOs, Odoo partners, and industrial companies looking to understand how Odoo can support not only digitalization, but also operational, financial and human transformation.

tracks.title: We built it for our Team. 14,000 people showed up. How Odoo helped us scale an unexpected EdTech Platform
tracks.speaker: Eddy BRUART from Heureia
tracks.speaker_raw: Eddy BRUART from Heureia
tracks.speaker_bio: Eddy Bruart is a Belgian digital entrepreneur and co-founder of Heure IA, a free AI certification platform that grew from an internal team training into a global initiative reaching 14,000+ users across 100+ countries in its first year. Built entirely on Odoo Online, Heure IA is aligned with the UNESCO AI Competency Framework. Eddy is the founder of Smartera, a digital growth agency, and co-founded Heure IA alongside Amra Zidani, founder of Agoraz, a certified Odoo Partner and his closest collaborator since 2020. Heure IA exhibited at the Odoo Experience Startup Village in 2025.
tracks.description:
It started with a simple idea between two co-founders: build a short AI training to get our own Agoraz team up to speed. No business plan. No revenue target. Just a practical need.
We built it on Odoo because that's what we already had. Website, eLearning module, user accounts, certifications. It was live in days. Then we decided to make it available publicly. For free. Still with no objective beyond "this might be useful to others."
One year later, Heure IA (www.heureia.com) has reached over 14,000 users across more than 100 countries. A Technical Operation Manager in Switzerland. A Financial Director in Algeria. A student in Burkina Faso. A professional in Cameroon who says she now uses AI every day at work. None of them paid a cent. None of them were in our plan. Because there was no plan.
What we want to share at Odoo Experience is an honest account of what two people with no dev team and no infrastructure budget actually built. From idea to live platform: four weeks. Website, eLearning module, user accounts, certification flows, CRM, Email Marketing. No custom development. No external tools. No agency. Just Odoo.
That time-to-market changed everything. It meant we could launch before the doubt set in, iterate in real time as users arrived from multiples countries, and focus entirely on the content because the platform never asked for our attention.
And now, one year in, the foundation Odoo gave us isn't just holding. It's the reason we can think about the next chapter without anxiety. Monetization, new modules, automated learner journeys, scaled content delivery: everything is already there, waiting to be activated. No re-platforming. No migration risk. No "we'll deal with that when we get there."
The lesson: Odoo didn't just help us launch. It gave a two-person team the architecture of a serious company, on day one.
Target audience: Odoo users, partners, startupers and entrepreneurs building on Odoo for content, education, or community platforms.
Key takeaway: What scaling without friction actually looks like. From 5 colleagues to 14,000 learners, on one Odoo instance.

tracks.speaker: Daniel Göppner
tracks.speaker_role: Principal Project Leader + Consultant at J.A. Daniel Göppner
tracks.speaker_raw: Daniel Göppner, Principal Project Leader + Consultant at J.A. Daniel Göppner
tracks.speaker_bio:
Daniel Göppner is a Principal Project Leader and Digital Advisor at braintec, and a seasoned Odoo expert with over 15 years of experience architecting complex ERP solutions. With a dual background in computer science and mathematics, Daniel approaches digital transformation from a deeply analytical perspective, seamlessly bridging the gap between high-level business strategy and deep-dive technical execution.
Throughout 8 years dedicated to the Odoo ecosystem, Daniel has guided 50+ successful implementations and holds certifications across 9+ Odoo versions. A seasoned veteran of the Odoo Experience stage (2019, 2024, 2025), he is recognized for his ability to translate intricate technical architectures into actionable business growth. Beyond Odoo, his expertise spans Python programming, Machine Learning, SEO optimization, and cybersecurity—reinforced by his credentials as a Harvard-certified Cybersecurity Risk Manager.
A true "multilingual" professional, Daniel navigates five human languages and five machine languages, ensuring that stakeholders and technology always speak the same language. Driven by his "J.A.D.G." philosophy—Journey, Acceleration, Digital Integrity, and Growth—his mission is to help the community build secure, innovative, and future-proof systems that turn Odoo from a software solution into a strategic engine for innovation.
tracks.description:
Can Odoo handle the specialized needs of the premium beverage industry?
Fine wine trading is a business of passion, but the back-office reality is one of extreme complexity. When dealing with rare bottles, "Differenzbesteuerung" (margin scheme taxation), and multi-company inventory, spreadsheets quickly become a liability.
In this session, we walk through the digital transformation of Trinkreif. We will explore how we moved from fragmented processes to a unified Odoo ecosystem that manages the entire lifecycle of a bottle—from global procurement and automated Anglo-Saxon accounting to CRM-driven sales.
We will deep-dive into the technical and financial hurdles we overcame:
- The Tax Puzzle: Mastering "Differenzbesteuerung" and complex VAT requirements.
- Precision Inventory: Why automated inventory valuation and Anglo-Saxon accounting are non-negotiable for high-value stock.
- The Multi-Company Flow: Seamlessly scaling operations without losing financial clarity.
- The Accountant’s Dream: How we collaborated with an Odoo-certified tax firm to ensure 100% compliance.
Whether you are a consultant or a business owner, you’ll leave with a blueprint for digitizing a traditional industry without losing its soul.

tracks.speaker_role: Senior Business Analyst at VentorTech at Ventor Tech

Incorrect analytic selections, inconsistent data entry, and limited reporting capabilities made managerial reports harder to trust.
This session explores how INEX redesigned its analytic accounting in Odoo to build a disciplined, rule-based management accounting system. The result was consistent data entry, precise multi-dimensional reporting, and a consolidated management view across the entire group.
KEY LEARNINGS
- Why flexible analytics alone are not enough for reliable managerial accounting
- Best practices for designing scalable analytic structures across multiple companies
- How guided analytic selection improves data quality and reporting accuracy
- Building precise multi-dimensional management reports in Odoo
- Creating a single source of truth across projects, business units, and legal entities
- Lessons learned from implementing advanced managerial accounting in a real multi-company organization
VALUE FOR THE AUDIENCE
Participants will gain practical insights into:
- Building reliable managerial accounting in Odoo for multi-company organizations
- Designing analytic structures that remain scalable as the business grows
- Improving the accuracy and trustworthiness of management reporting
- Common implementation pitfalls and how to avoid them
- Best practices for collaboration between business teams and Odoo consultants
TARGET AUDIENCE
This talk is ideal for:
- Owners and executives of large groups of companies
- IT Managers overseeing enterprise platforms
- CFOs and finance leaders assessing ERP transitions
- Project Managers from client and vendor sides
- Odoo Partners working with international and enterprise clients

tracks.title: From Excel to Odoo 19: Advancing ERP & CRM Maturity for a Multi-Entity Group.
tracks.speaker: Thomas Deville
tracks.speaker_role: Chief Financial Officer at Alteo Group
tracks.speaker_raw: Thomas Deville, Chief Financial Officer at Alteo Group
tracks.speaker_bio: Thomas Deville, aged 40, describes himself as the coordinator of a collective of entrepreneurs committed to sustainability. After studying civil engineering alongside a complementary master’s degree in management and entrepreneurship, he quickly found his niche in this coordinating role, taking on responsibilities as a team leader, operations manager, finance manager and recruitment manager. In 2018, he was commissioned by the engineering consultancy Deplasse to coordinate the implementation of an ERP system. Thomas currently serves as managing director of the ALTEO Group and as financial director for all the group’s subsidiaries. In these two roles, he oversees the group’s internal coordination and ensures the well-being of the ALTEO Group’s 150 employees.
tracks.description:
Deplasse & Associés, a consultancy specialising in building technology and environmental advice, began its digital transformation in 2018 by moving away from Excel spreadsheets in favour of Odoo. Since then, the ALTEO Group — now comprising eight entities active in environmental transition and offering a wide range of services throughout a building’s life cycle — has gradually integrated all its activities into a single Odoo instance, hosted in-house thanks to the technical expertise of AISET, a group member that develops a SaaS solution for managing the technical, legal and energy-related aspects of buildings.   This presentation traces this journey: the successes, but also the mistakes made in the implementation and management of an ERP-CRM system — notably an excessive reliance on custom developments that compromised maintenance and version upgrades, which began with our launch in 2018 using the ‘community’ version. The major turning point: the return to the standard Odoo version in August 2025, accompanied by in-depth work carried out in collaboration with Odoo on documenting and simplifying processes. The result: increasingly comprehensive and user-friendly use of the system (accounting in January 2026, followed gradually by the fleet, websites, leave and other modules), an in-house update to v19 in February 2026, accounting in January 2026, and significantly improved stability.   Key takeaways: why the standard Odoo architecture is often the best long-term solution; why it is important to document, communicate and adapt processes internally; how to strike the right balance between internal resources, an integrator and direct Odoo support. Value for the audience: concrete, unfiltered insights from eight years of deployment — the choices made and their operational consequences. Target audience: executives and IT managers at multi-entity SMEs, Odoo users wishing to move away from technical customisation debt, and any organisation in the process of upgrading.   Timeline: - Before 2018 — 100% decentralised Excel-based management - 2018 — Odoo deployment in v11 Community (Deplasse & Associés), on-premises hosting - 2022 — Upgrade to v15 with an external integrator (relatively painful); introduction of A+ Concept (implemented in-house – also relatively difficult due to technical legacy issues) - 2023 — Integration of CUB3 (starting from scratch – simplicity) - 2024 — Expansion to AISET, FANDO, Freestone and ForABetterCapital (carried out in-house, learning experience, some drawbacks but generally successful) - Spring 2025 — Odoo support (Matthieu Tans) to return to the standard; documentation and simplification of internal processes - August 2025 — In-house migration to v18 (no custom development; lightweight modules only); server and security management taken over by AISET - January 2026 — Odoo accounting for all entities; return of an external integrator as backup (Agitech) + Introduction of Peppol (opportunity for 100% invoice management on Odoo) - February 2026 — Migration to v19 - Spring 2026 — Ongoing work to standardise practices: products, contacts, filters, email templates, field names, etc. - April 2026 — Integration of BRAFT. A team of AI experts

tracks.title: How a US Tobacco Distributor Replaced MS Dynamics and QuickBooks with One Odoo System
tracks.speaker: Jainesh Shah
tracks.speaker_role: Co-founder and Director at Aktiv Software Inc
tracks.speaker_raw: Jainesh Shah, Co-founder and Director at Aktiv Software Inc
tracks.speaker_bio: As a Co-founder & Director at Aktiv Software, Jainesh Shah turns client requirements into Odoo solutions built to last and to scale. He is at his strongest where the requirement is not a standard feature but a set of strict, real-world rules that have to be encoded correctly, which is exactly what the tobacco trade demands.
tracks.description:
About Mega Wholesale:
- Mega Wholesale is a tobacco and cigarette distribution company in the United States.
- It ran on MS Dynamics, QuickBooks, and several other disconnected tools that did not talk to each other.
- The hardest parts of the trade were slow and error-prone: state tax-stamp compliance, multi-location stock, and tax reporting.
- The goal was to replace the entire legacy stack with a single ERP.
What this session covers:
- Mega Wholesale's move from MS Dynamics and QuickBooks to Odoo, and the distribution solution Aktiv built around the strict compliance rules of the tobacco trade.
- Discovery and solution blueprinting, and replacing several disconnected systems with one connected platform.
- A custom tax-stamp engine tightly integrated with Sales and Inventory.
- The result: the correct state tax stamp is detected and applied automatically on the sales order, the right quantity is calculated from the product's pack data, and stamp stock is deducted on delivery, removing the manual work and compliance risk of handling stamps outside the ERP.
- Location-aware stock that keeps cigarettes and tobacco in separate locations.
- Automatic stock allocation with safeguards against misallocation.
- Permit tracking for every distributor.
- Shelf-life management by expiration date.
- State-wise tax and VAT reporting.
Who should attend:
- Teams in regulated distribution.
- Anyone replacing a patchwork of multiple disconnected tools and spreadsheets with one ERP.
What attendees will learn
- How to replace MS Dynamics, QuickBooks, and other legacy tools with a single Odoo system without losing compliance control.
- How to automate state-wise tax-stamp detection, quantity calculation, and stock deduction directly on the sales order.
- How location-aware stock and automatic allocation rules prevent misplaced inventory across separate cigarette and tobacco locations.
- How permit tracking, shelf-life management, and delivery restrictions keep a regulated distribution business audit-ready.

tracks.title: From SME to Enterprise: How We Pushed Odoo Security Beyond the Defaults (and What Broke Along the Way)
tracks.speaker: Rutger Hofste
tracks.speaker_raw: Rutger Hofste, CTO at Pantalytics B.V.
tracks.speaker_bio:
Rutger Hofste is a data scientist and entrepreneur focused on secure, AI powered business systems built on Odoo. He works with SME+ and enterprise clients in strategically sensitive industries, helping them scale Odoo to meet higher security and identity management requirements. As founder of Pantalytics, he develops advanced solutions around Odoo, AI, and security, including email hardening, SSO, automated user provisioning, and enterprise grade access control on Odoo.sh and Odoo Enterprise.
Rutger combines a strong analytical background from TU Delft and the National University of Singapore with hands on experience building production ready systems. His work bridges real client demands with responsible security practices, including responsible disclosure and upstream contributions to the Odoo ecosystem.
tracks.description:
As Odoo increasingly moves upmarket, security expectations rise sharply. In this talk we share a real world journey with an SME+ client (€25-100m revenue) operating in a strategically sensitive industry. For them, the default Odoo Enterprise and Odoo.sh security setup was not sufficient to meet internal and external requirements.
Starting from concrete client feedback, we systematically strengthened Odoo’s security. We enhanced outgoing and incoming email security, implemented robust SSO and automated user provisioning, and aligned identity and access management with enterprise standards. This work resulted in a reusable set of custom security modules that elevate Odoo.sh (Enterprise) to a level suitable for larger and more security conscious customers.
This session is practical, transparent, and forward looking, showing how Odoo can confidently win larger clients without compromising on security or openness.

tracks.title: How AI transforms ERP into a proactive sales tool: the Jacques Remy case study.
tracks.speaker: Louis Berwart
tracks.speaker_raw: Louis Berwart, Data Manager at Idealis Consulting
tracks.speaker_bio: Dedicated to driving data-driven success, Louis combines strategic vision with hands-on analytical expertise. His focus on making advanced data insights accessible empowers clients to make informed decisions.
tracks.description:
In the fresh food distribution industry, demand uncertainty is the primary driver of margin loss. How can you guarantee maximum product availability without the constant risk of overstocking? The answer lies in the intelligent exploitation of data.
Discover the real-world success story of Jacques Remy, a leading wholesaler that integrated Artificial Intelligence into the core of its Odoo ERP with the strategic support of Idealis. By processing over 400,000 historical sales records, we co-developed a system capable of modeling supermarket purchasing behavior to anticipate their actual needs before they even place an order.
This talk will deep dive into the implementation of a hybrid AI engine. Moving beyond theoretical hype, we will explain how we correlated Odoo transactional data with critical external variables—such as local weather, seasonality, and public calendars—to automatically generate draft orders with unprecedented accuracy.
Key takeaways from this session:
- Data Engineering: How to extract high-value insights from Odoo history using BigQuery.
- "Stock-Aware" Logic: How the AI adjusts its predictions based on real-time warehouse availability and suggests intelligent substitutions ("Star Products").
- Operational Impact: Shifting from reactive logistics to a proactive "push-flow" strategy, backed by Jacques Remy’s real KPIs.
Join us to see how Idealis is pushing the boundaries of Odoo, transforming it into a predictive performance engine for supply chain leaders. A session focused on ROI, scalability, and technical feasibility.

tracks.title: Inside the Box or Best of Breed: Architecting eCommerce on Odoo
tracks.speaker: Nico Ziemski from ruhrdot GmbH
tracks.speaker_raw: Nico Ziemski from ruhrdot GmbH
tracks.description:
Odoo's eCommerce vision is beautifully integrated: build the storefront in Odoo Website, sell on marketplaces through native connectors, ship with built-in carrier integrations, and keep the books in the same system. For many businesses that all-in-one path is exactly right. But a large share of mid-market merchants arrive with a different reality: a high-converting storefront already running on Shopify, Shopware or WooCommerce; sales spread across Amazon, Otto, Kaufland and eBay. Money landing through PayPal, Stripe, Klarna. Fulfillment outsourced to a third-party logistics provider and non-negotiable accounting rules. This talk is a neutral field playbook drawn from ruhrdot. projects that process up to 100,000 invoices and 35,000 shipments on a peak day. For each building block we contrast how Odoo intends it to work with the architecture you actually build when the storefront and channels live outside Odoo: connecting external shops, orchestrating marketplaces through middleware, matching payouts back to orders and invoices when money flow does not equal order flow, integrating shipping carriers like DHL and GLS plus a third-party logistics provider, and producing clean, preparatory accounting with period locks, document hashing and the correct chart of accounts. We also show the per-channel logging modules that keep every shop auditable. Attendees leave with a decision framework for what belongs natively in Odoo versus an integration, where to place the seams, and how to keep accounting audit-proof no matter how many shops and marketplaces feed the system.
<div

The solution also covers multi currency operations, dual exchange rate handling, automated quality inspections, and standardized financial reporting across regional requirements.
The result is stronger cost transparency, cleaner financial accuracy, better compliance control, and a scalable manufacturing foundation where production, quality, and finance move together with confidence.

tracks.speaker_raw: Jean-François Noel & Ewa Deka, Assistant Head Advisory of the Internal Control Capability Unit (JF Noel) & Business Manager (Ewa) at tsc - The Service Company SRL
tracks.speaker_bio: Formation en comptabilité et obtenu une licence en gestion d’entreprise. J’ai ensuite travaillé depuis quinze ans dans divers secteurs, principalement la consultance et le secteur financier. Je travaille à présent pour les Écoles Européennes.
tracks.description:
Abstract
How do you successfully implement Odoo for more than 4,000 users across 14 European Schools while ensuring a consistent user experience and standardized business processes?
This talk focuses on the challenges that begin once the project kicks off.
The European Schools project is one of the largest Odoo implementations in terms of user count. The initial scope covers the deployment of the complete Odoo HR suite to support the management of teachers across all schools, with the goal of harmonizing HR processes at an international level.
Through this real-life case study, we will share the key decisions and lessons learned from the early stages of the project, including:
Structuring a project designed for more than 4,000 users.
Managing an international deployment involving 14 schools.
Supporting the customer in standardizing business processes across organizations with different historical ways of working.
Designing an effective governance model, including user roles and access rights.
Helping end users embrace a solution they had never used before.
Making key architectural decisions, such as choosing between a single shared database and one database per school, and why we ultimately selected a single database.
Organizing the implementation with a pilot phase followed by a structured roll-out across all schools.
The functional scope already delivered includes the Odoo HR suite:
Employees
Recruitment
Appraisals
Attendances
Overtime management
Onboarding & Offboarding
Requests
Payroll preparation
Today, more than 1,000 users are actively using the solution.
This session will present the key lessons learned from the first phase of the project, the challenges we faced, the mistakes to avoid, and the best practices for successfully delivering an Odoo implementation at this scale.
As the project is still ongoing, this talk will be the first chapter of our journey. We plan to return at Odoo Experience 2027 to present the complete deployment across all 14 European Schools, share user feedback, and discuss the lessons learned from the full rollout.

tracks.title: Boosting Quality Control with Odoo: Migrating from Asana to Odoo for integrated quality management workflow
tracks.speaker: Kushal Darji
tracks.speaker_role: Manager, Customer Success at Surekha Technologies Pvt. Ltd.
tracks.speaker_raw: Kushal Darji, Manager, Customer Success at Surekha Technologies Pvt. Ltd.
tracks.speaker_bio:
As a Manager of Customer Success, I work closely with clients to ensure they are able to use Odoo effectively in their day-to-day operations. My role involves guiding customers through implementation, supporting them as they grow, and helping them solve challenges along the way.
I believe in keeping things simple and practical, focusing on what truly works for the customer. Through my experience, I’ve seen how the right approach to customer success can make a big difference. At Odoo Expo, I’m excited to share a few real examples and insights that others can easily relate to and apply.
tracks.description:
A space-tech company was managing quality processes and task tracking across Asana and other disconnected tools, resulting in poor data visibility, manual coordination, and limited traceability between customer issues and production. To address this, a fully integrated solution was developed in Odoo, connecting Helpdesk, Quality, and Manufacturing into a unified workflow. Quality Alerts are automatically triggered from Helpdesk tickets and Quality Checks, ensuring real-time synchronization of data across modules.
We helped in providing the source and context of each alert, enabling more accurate and structured data capture for quality checks. We also introduced the structured root cause analysis through an interactive Fishbone diagram and enforced production control by automatically locking Manufacturing and Work Orders when quality issues are detected.
Additionally, dynamic COC documents are generated using configurable templates, allowing users to complete and sign them within Odoo. An audit logging mechanism tracks user actions such as deletion and archiving with mandatory reasons, ensuring accountability.
Based on client feedback, this implementation reduced manual effort by approximately 70% and improved issue resolution time by around 60%, delivering a fully automated, traceable, and compliance-ready system.

We’ll also dive into maintenance planning with the Gantt view, showing how teams can schedule preventive and corrective work while balancing resources and minimizing operational disruption.
Beyond day-to-day execution, we’ll look at the financial side of maintenance: budgeting and tracking maintenance costs, understanding the real cost of keeping equipment running, and using that information to support better asset management decisions. We’ll also explore how AI can assist maintenance teams during operations by providing real-time troubleshooting suggestions. From organizing maintenance activities to deciding when repairing a machine no longer makes financial sense, this session demonstrates how Odoo 20 can help maintenance teams turn operational data into smarter decisions and keep their assets running efficiently.

tracks.title: „From Readiness to Rollout: How Hinz&Kunzt Prepared a Complex ERP Transformation with Odoo“
tracks.speaker: Christiane Grothus
tracks.speaker_raw: Christiane Grothus, Managing Director at Opalis
tracks.speaker_bio: Christiane Grothues is Managing Director of Opalis Consulting GmbH and brings many years of experience in organizational transformation, governance, process management and change enablement. Throughout her career, she has held leadership roles as consultant, partner, authorized signatory and managing director. Before starting at and ultimately leading Opalis, she worked in senior governance and data protection roles at companies like Logwin AG (then Thiel Logistik) and DNV (then Germanischer Lloyd and DNV GL). In transformation projects, she helps organizations build clarity, readiness and sustainable decision-making structures before implementation starts.
tracks.description:
Implementing a new ERP system is never just about software — especially not when long-established processes, specific organizational requirements and a complex operating model come together. In this session, Hinz&Kunzt, Opalis Consulting and Intero will jointly share how an Odoo project can be successfully prepared and launched when clarity, readiness and stakeholder alignment are just as important as the technical solution itself. The talk focuses on how an organization with a unique operating model can move towards a future-proof ERP platform. It highlights key thematic areas such as mapping core business processes in Odoo, addressing specific functional requirements, integrating relevant interfaces, preparing data migration, and setting up structured testing, training and project governance. These areas reflect the main functional project topics identified during the preparation phase. A particularly valuable angle of this story is the preparation phase before implementation: Opalis supported Hinz&Kunzt in shaping the transformation, moderating the selection process, preparing the organization from a change-management perspective and, after an unsuccessful first attempt with another Odoo partner, connecting the organization with Intero. This makes the session more than a software success story — it becomes a practical case about readiness, partner selection and the conditions required for successful ERP transformation. Attendees will gain actionable insights into the success factors of a more complex Odoo rollout, the interaction between organizational readiness and implementation, and the importance of setting up the right project foundations from the very beginning.

tracks.title: Consolidating the Stack: Replacing WooCommerce with Native Odoo Enterprise eCommerce Extensions
tracks.speaker: Tomás Van Loock
tracks.speaker_raw: Tomás Van Loock, ERP Consultant   at much. Consulting
tracks.speaker_bio: Tomás Van Loock is an AI & BI ERP Consultant at much. Consulting. Combining a background in Data Science and Management, he approaches Odoo Enterprise as a unified ecosystem rather than a collection of siloed applications. His implementation portfolio spans Manufacturing, Field Service, and eCommerce architectures. This broad horizontal system expertise allows him to bypass module constraints and map intricate business requirements into natively integrated Odoo frameworks.
tracks.description:
B2B2B hardware resellers frequently suffer from fragmented digital architectures, forcing them to maintain complex integrations between external platforms like WooCommerce and their core ERP system. For Cisco Meraki distributor Cloud Controlled, this ecosystem disconnect resulted in constant manual data synchronization, isolated product specifications, and a critical inability to track mandatory end-user data during the standard checkout process.
By migrating the entire operation to the Odoo Enterprise eCommerce and Website apps, we eliminated the WooCommerce middleware entirely and built directly on top of the native ERP data structure. We extended the core Odoo architecture to enable nested category inheritance for deep technical specifications, implemented dynamic real-time fetching of customer lead times directly from standard inventory models, and built a customized B2B2B checkout flow that captures required end-user delivery addresses for reseller compliance automatically.
This single Odoo environment permanently removed the need to sync separate platforms or update web catalogs by hand. Automatically pushing technical data to the storefront cut out hours of weekly admin work on lead times. It also reduced routine technical inquiries, meaning the sales team spent significantly less time answering basic hardware questions.
Key Points of this Talk:
- Removing WooCommerce: Replacing external web shop middleware with native Odoo Enterprise eCommerce apps.
- Smart Product Categories: Extending Odoo's category model so subcategories automatically inherit technical data.
- Live Lead Times: Automatically pulling real-time customer lead times from inventory straight to the website frontend.
- Strict B2B2B Checkout: Changing the regular Odoo eCommerce checkout flow to enforce mandatory end-user address tracking.
- Automatic Data Flow: Letting product specifications automatically pass through complex nested subcategories.
Key Learnings:
- Why you should eliminate external eCommerce integrations by leveraging native Odoo Website architecture.
- How to extend Odoo category models to propagate complex technical data automatically.
- How to dynamically expose backend inventory lead times to the frontend customer experience.
- How to customize the Odoo checkout process to capture multi-tier reseller data, incl. end user information.
Target Audience:
Technical Sales Leads, Solutions Architects, Senior Python Devs, and Technical Leads using Odoo Enterprise v18 and onwards.

tracks.title: From CAD to Manufacturing: Connecting SOLIDWORKS, 3DEXPERIENCE and Odoo into One Digital Thread
tracks.speaker: Tero Salonen
tracks.speaker_role: Product Director at ATR Soft Oy
tracks.speaker_raw: Tero Salonen, Product Director at ATR Soft Oy
tracks.speaker_bio: Tero Salonen is Product Director at ATR Soft. He has worked at ATR Soft since 2000, starting as a software developer and later moving into product management and international integration projects. With a Master’s degree in Engineering and extensive experience in CAD, PDM, PLM, and ERP integrations, he helps manufacturing companies connect engineering systems such as SOLIDWORKS, SOLIDWORKS PDM, and 3DEXPERIENCE with business platforms like Odoo. Tero has previously presented ATR CustomTools and Odoo integration at Odoo Experience and regularly shares practical insights from real customer projects.
tracks.description:
Manufacturing companies often struggle with disconnected processes between engineering, purchasing, and production. Product data is created in CAD, PDM, or PLM systems, but turning that information into products, bills of materials, manufacturing orders, purchase requirements, and controlled product changes in ERP is still often manual, error-prone, and difficult to scale.
In this session, Tero Salonen from ATR Soft will show how manufacturers can connect SOLIDWORKS, SOLIDWORKS PDM, 3DEXPERIENCE, and Odoo into one practical digital thread from engineering to manufacturing. Building on ATR CustomTools’ experience from real-world Odoo–SOLIDWORKS integration projects, the presentation will go beyond simple import and export of product data. It will demonstrate how engineering information can be used in Odoo to create and update products and BOMs, support manufacturing order creation, enable purchase processes for buy components, and help manage engineering changes across systems.
The audience will learn how CAD and PLM data can support operational processes in Odoo, what to consider when planning an integration project, and how to avoid common pitfalls when connecting engineering and ERP systems. The session is especially valuable for manufacturing companies using Odoo together with SOLIDWORKS, SOLIDWORKS PDM, or 3DEXPERIENCE, as well as professionals working in engineering, production planning, purchasing, product data management, or business process development.
ATR CustomTools has been positioned around automating SOLIDWORKS and Odoo data flows, including product and BOM creation, previews, drawings, and comparison of changes between SOLIDWORKS and Odoo.

tracks.title: Killing the 8 Wastes: A Functional Blueprint for Lean Manufacturing in Odoo Enterprise
tracks.speaker: Nuhash Kinzel
tracks.speaker_role: Senior Solutions Consultant at much. Consulting
tracks.speaker_raw: Nuhash Kinzel, Senior Solutions Consultant at much. Consulting
tracks.speaker_bio: Nuhash Kinzel is a Senior Solutions Consultant at much. Consulting in Munich. With four years of experience at a leading Odoo Gold Partner, Nuhash has supported over 100 business transformation projects, specializing in the conceptualization and architectural planning of complex operations. He has personally supported the functional and technical setup of over 30 Odoo implementations, focusing on scaling manufacturing and logistics through data-driven Lean methodologies.
tracks.description:
The "Hidden Factory"—the accumulation of non-value-added activities—accounts for up to 40% of operational costs in mid-sized manufacturing.
To remain competitive, companies must actively attack the eight Lean wastes (TIMWOODS). This talk provides a concrete implementation plan to weaponize Odoo Enterprise MRP and Inventory against these inefficiencies, transforming the shop floor from a cost center into a high-throughput engine.
We will outline how we used Odoo Enterprise Barcoding to eliminate unnecessary Motion and Transportation, alongside the Shop Floor App to resolve Waiting and Overprocessing through real-time Work Instructions. After, we will explore the "Skills" gap, showing how to restrict complex operations to certified personnel via Work Center logic. Finally, we will showcase how to expose "Hidden Waste" by extracting status-based transition data into an external BI Data Warehouse. By leveraging Odoo's native data structure, we demonstrate how one partner achieved a 20% reduction in lead times and a 15% increase in Overall Equipment Effectiveness (OEE) by identifying bottlenecks that standard ERP reporting often overlooks.
Key Points of this Talk:
- Inventory Waste: Implementing Make to Order (MTO) and Master Production Schedule (MPS) logic to eliminate overproduction and capital lock-up.
- Motion & Transportation: Deploying Odoo Barcoding to automate internal transfers and bin-to-bin movements.
- Defect Control: Integrating Quality Control Points (QCP) directly into the manufacturing routing sequence.
- Skill Management: Restricting Work Center access based on Employee Skill levels and certifications.
- Waiting Times: Using the Shop Floor Tablet interface for paperless, real-time job queuing.
- Waste Analytics: Exporting status-based Odoo data via Extract, Transform, Load (ETL) pipelines to Superset for bottleneck visualization.
Key Learnings:
- How to map the 8 TIMWOODS wastes to specific Odoo Enterprise functional settings.
- How to configure automated Quality Checks to prevent the "Flow of Defects."
- How to use Odoo Barcoding to reduce physical movement in high-volume warehouses.
- How to leverage Odoo Work Instructions to reduce the training period for new staff.
- How to identify "Waiting" waste by analyzing Work Order status transitions in BI.
Target Audience:
- Operations Managers looking to implement Lean methodologies.
- Production Planners using Odoo Enterprise MRP v18/v19.
- Functional Consultants designing complex manufacturing processes.

tracks.speaker_raw: Jérôme Belpaire (beje), Software Developer at Odoo
tracks.description:
Leaving files scattered in the chatter is fine when they are not essential to an app's workflow, but when those files are important, things can easily get messy. Integrating the Documents app brings much-needed structure, making files easier to organize, secure, and use.

The Setup: Hooking up a custom model to the Documents app so file uploads are captured correctly.
Organization: Automatically generating subfolders and assigning tags based on the record's context.
