tracks.title: Automating 30,000 Members: Translating Complex NPO Fee Matrices into Odoo Enterprise Subscriptions
tracks.speaker: Nicolas Colsman
tracks.speaker_raw: Nicolas Colsman, CEO at ZdoV GmbH
tracks.speaker_bio: Nicolas Colsman (Spiegel Bestselling Author, expert for the digitalization of states, NGOs, and Faith-Based Organizations, and CEO of ZdoV - Zukunft digitale und offene Verwaltung GmbH
tracks.description:
Managing a 30,000-member association in Germany traditionally mandates heavy administrative overhead, particularly when membership dues are dictated by convoluted variables like academic degrees, membership tenure, and specialized research grants. Historically, processing these nested logic trees required legacy databases, fractured Excel sheets, and 2.5 full-time equivalents (FTEs) purely dedicated to billing and reconciliation.
To eliminate this bottleneck, ZdoV architected a centralized association framework utilizing Odoo Enterprise Contacts, Subscriptions, and Accounting. We developed custom calculation logic to inherit the intricate legacy fee matrix and map it directly onto dynamic Odoo subscription products. This architecture programmatically executes the entire financial lifecycle: it calculates the precise variable fee per member, automates recurring invoicing, processes high-volume SEPA Direct Debit mandates natively within the accounting module, and generates legally compliant German donation receipts (Spendenbescheinigungen) without manual intervention.
By replacing disconnected legacy systems with a unified Odoo Enterprise environment, the association fundamentally restructured its operational efficiency. The automated billing and SEPA reconciliation cycle reduced the required administrative overhead from 2.5 FTEs down to a 0.5 FTE workload, proving Odoo's capacity to handle massive, highly localized non-profit constraints.
Key Points of this Talk:
- Mapping legacy variable fee matrices (academic degrees, grants) to Odoo Subscriptions.
- Centralizing 30,000 member records within Odoo Enterprise Contacts to deprecate Excel.
- Executing high-volume SEPA Direct Debit mandates via Odoo Enterprise Accounting.
- Automating the generation of compliant German donation receipts (Spendenbescheinigungen).
- Reducing billing administration workload from 2.5 to 0.5 FTEs.
Key Learnings:
- How to translate intricate legacy calculation parameters into dynamic Odoo subscription products.
- How to configure Odoo Accounting for high-volume, automated SEPA reconciliation.
- How to structure Odoo Contacts to handle complex non-profit membership hierarchies.
Target Audience:
Functional Consultants, NPO Administrators, and Solution Architects using Odoo Enterprise.

tracks.title: From NetSuite to Odoo: How a 50-Year-Old Meat-Processing Equipment Maker Unified CPQ, Manufacturing and Inventory
tracks.speaker: Devang Mehta
tracks.speaker_role: Co-founder and Director of Operations at Aktiv Software
tracks.speaker_raw: Devang Mehta, Co-founder and Director of Operations at Aktiv Software
tracks.speaker_bio: Devang Mehta is the Co-founder and Director of Operations at Aktiv Software, bringing over 15 years of experience in operations management and customer success. He oversees project delivery across teams, keeping timelines, quality, and communication aligned so that what a client signs up for is what they actually receive.
tracks.description:
Kentmaster has built meat-processing equipment for over 50 years, with operations across the United States, Australia, Ireland, South Africa, China, and Argentina. As the business scaled, NetSuite's rising licensing costs and limited flexibility became a real constraint, while quoting, manufacturing, and inventory ran across disconnected tools that slowed the business down.
This session walks through Kentmaster's migration from NetSuite to Odoo and the configure-to-order solution Aktiv built around it. We will cover the full journey: discovery and solution blueprinting, a large-scale data migration of thousands of products, variants, and complex BoMs with no disruption to operations, and a custom CPQ module tightly integrated with Sales and Manufacturing. The result is a single flow where a confirmed quote automatically generates the correct BoM and routes it to production, removing the rework and pricing inconsistencies that came from quoting outside the ERP.
Beyond CPQ, we will show how location-aware manufacturing, preferred-location inventory rules with serial traceability, and an automated order-to-cash flow came together into one connected system, giving leadership real-time visibility across multiple companies for the first time.
Attendees evaluating a migration from a costly proprietary ERP, or manufacturers struggling to connect quoting to production, will leave with a practical reference for how this is done on Odoo.
What attendees will learn:
- How to plan and execute a large-scale NetSuite-to-Odoo migration without disrupting live operations
- How CPQ can drive accurate quotes and automatic BoM creation straight into manufacturing
- How location-aware production and preferred-location inventory rules improve accuracy across multiple warehouses
- What a connected quote-to-production-to-invoice flow looks like in practice
<div

tracks.title: Beyond Serial Numbers: Automating High-Volume Software Licensing in Odoo Enterprise.
tracks.speaker: Lisa Adamy
tracks.speaker_raw: Lisa Adamy, ERP Consultant at much. Consulting
tracks.speaker_bio: As a Services ERP Consultant at much. Consulting, Lisa Adamy focuses on optimizing day-to-day operations for service organizations using Odoo Enterprise. She transforms complex business requirements into intuitive, highly automated digital architectures that drive sustainable growth.
tracks.description:
Software distributors face a unique structural paradox in Odoo: they require the traceability of serial numbers without the overhead of physical inventory moves. Arina, a leading European provider of digital forensics tools, struggled with a fragmented "Order-to-Cash" flow where license keys were manually copy-pasted across Sales Orders, Purchase Orders, and Subscriptions, leading to significant data decay and renewal leakage. To solve this, a centralized license.key architecture was deployed, leveraging Odoo Enterprise Subscription logic to create a persistent digital asset thread.
By inheriting standard Enterprise methods such as _prepare_invoice_line and _get_renew_upsell_values, the system ensures that license keys persist automatically through the entire lifecycle - from the initial RFQ to annual upsells. This deep integration allows for "Back-to-Back" procurement, where purchase prices are secured before Sales Order confirmation, a critical requirement for high-margin software distribution. The result is a 80% reduction in administrative overhead, managing over 1,000 active subscriptions with zero manual data duplication between procurement and accounting.
In this talk, we will cover:
- Digital Asset Centralization: Why standard stock.production.lot fails for intangible goods and how to replace it.
- Subscription Persistence: Using license_key_ids to maintain traceability during Odoo Enterprise renewal and upsell cycles.
- Automated Procurement Flow: Triggering RFQs via custom product flags to secure margins before SO confirmation.
- The Mixin Architecture: Deploying license.key.mixin to unify headers and lines across SO, PO, and Invoicing.
- Reporting & Transparency: Dynamic injection of license data into PDF templates for quotes, invoices, and delivery slips.
- Order-to-Cash Efficiency: Reducing manual intervention by 70% for complex forensic software distribution.
You will learn:
- How to manage non-storable assets that require unique identifiers without triggering stock moves.
- How to extend Odoo Enterprise Subscription logic to carry custom relational data into upsell and renewal orders.
- How to automate the "Back-to-Back" vendor procurement process for services and digital goods.
- How to avoid data silos by using a single source of truth for license expiration and payment dates.
- How to architect a modular Mixin that ensures consistent data flow across all accounting documents.
Target Audience:
- Odoo Partners & Consultants managing software or SaaS distribution clients.
- CFOs & Operations Managers using Odoo Enterprise Subscriptions.
- Intermediate Developers interested in extending Subscription and Procurement logic (v18/v19).

tracks.title: Empowering the Portal: Let Your Clients Self-Service and Save Your Team Time
tracks.speaker: Gin Yan
tracks.speaker_raw: Gin Yan, Business Advisor at Sodexis, Inc.
tracks.speaker_bio: After earning his Bachelor’s degree in Marketing and International Business from the State University of New York at Oswego, Gin built a formidable track record in the ERP industry. He spent several years within the manufacturing and distribution sectors to master the fundamentals of business operations. Bringing extensive retail and wholesale experience, he joined the Sodexis team in early 2025. He initially served as a Business Analyst to master the technical intricacies of Odoo implementations before stepping into his current leadership role. Today, Gin leads our US Sales Operations, combining deep technical analysis with sharp commercial expertise.
tracks.description:
Discover how to optimize Odoo’s customer portal to give your clients 24/7 access to their data, reducing administrative overhead and speeding up business cycles.
Your customer service and sales teams likely spend hours every week responding to routine emails. They are stuck sending copy-paste invoice PDFs, tracking down shipping numbers, or manually updating customers on order statuses. This back-and-forth slows your team down, and it forces your clients to wait on an email response just to get basic information about their own accounts.
We solve this bottleneck by leaning into Odoo’s native customer portal and tailoring it to act as a true self-service hub. Instead of treating the portal as an afterthought, we configure it so your clients can log in 24/7 to securely view their order history, download invoices, pay outstanding balances, and track shipments in real time. For businesses with recurring revenue models, we can even allow customers to manage their own subscriptions or submit support tickets directly through their dashboard, which automatically routes the data right into your Odoo backend.
Giving your clients direct access does not mean losing control. It simply removes the friction from the process. By shifting routine tasks to a secure self-service portal, you give your customers the instant answers they want while freeing up your team to focus on higher-value work.

tracks.speaker_role: Director of Implementation at Sodexis, Inc.

tracks.speaker_bio: Cecilie Barreto earned her bachelor of science in computer engineering from the University of Central Florida in 2018. Are you struggling to manage financial consolidations across multiple entities and currencies?

Enter Odoo V19! Odoo’s latest localization and accounting enhancements enable seamless real-time data synchronization across borders, thereby solving the complex multi-company and multi-country consolidation problem for expanding businesses.
This technology eliminates the need for manual spreadsheets and tedious external reporting tools. Over the past years, our team has successfully streamlined complex international accounting structures, enabling financial departments to reduce their closing times. With Odoo 19’s advanced multi-currency revaluation and centralized dashboard, multi-national groups can now manage dozens of legal entities with full transparency and compliance.
Join this session to discover how growing enterprises have achieved remarkable efficiency in their global operations—and how Odoo 19’s newest consolidation features play a key role in reaching these milestones.

tracks.title: Mastering subcontracting in Odoo 20: Best practices and new features for externalized production
tracks.speaker: Piet Gruyters
tracks.speaker_raw: Piet Gruyters, Business Analyst at Odoo
tracks.speaker_bio: Piet Gruyters  is a Services for Partners Consultant at Odoo, where he has spent 6 years leading Odoo implementations of all sizes, managing teams, and training both employees and partners. He has extensive experience advising SMEs & mid-market companies including manufacturing, pharmaceutical, and construction businesses on how to best use Odoo to manage and improve their business operations.
tracks.description:
Beyond the Standard Flow: Mastering Subcontracting in Odoo
Outsourcing manufacturing operations has become standard practice for businesses ranging from startups to mid-sized enterprises, yet many Odoo users believe there is only one standard way to handle subcontracting. This presentation demonstrates three distinct, real-world workflows tailored to different operational needs and vendor relationships:
Subcontractor Portal Collaboration : Grant external vendors portal access to log lot and serial numbers directly, establishing tight traceability for high-spec component manufacturing. PO-less Subcontracting & Direct Costing : Streamline high-frequency subcontracted steps—such as packaging—by recording stock movements and absorbing service costs directly into inventory valuation without generating Purchase Orders. Full 3PL & Complete Outsourcing : Manage complete manufacturing outsourcing for companies that control product BOMs and component sourcing, utilizing BOM Overview purchasing, subcontractor location replenishment, and dropshipping. At the end, you will leave with practical examples on how to tailor Odoo's subcontracting capabilities to your specific supply chain requirements.

tracks.title: Customer success story: Artel Rubber's Engineer-to-Order Transformation with Odoo
tracks.speaker: Giovanni Ughi
tracks.speaker_raw: Giovanni Ughi, CEO at BRYO GmbH
tracks.speaker_bio: Giovanni founded BRYO in 2023 to help manufacturers of complex industrial products transform their operations. Before BRYO, Giovanni was COO of a German manufacturing marketplace, supplying custom parts to leading OEMs like Schunk, Schuler and German Bionic.
tracks.description:
In this talk, the CEO of Bryo shares the story of the digital transformation at Artel Rubber, the UK’s leading manufacturer of silicon hoses for complex industrial applications. This is not a standard ERP implementation story, but a journey through complexity, failed attempts, and a breakthrough enabled by Odoo.
Artel Rubber operates in an engineer-to-order environment, where every product is designed and manufactured based on customer requirements. This creates a high level of complexity in one of the most critical business processes: designing, quoting and manufacturing custom products.
The key challenge is to define a new bill of materials within the ERP system for each new design. Each bill of materials includes different operations distributed across six work centres and consists of multiple components and raw materials.
For years, this challenge blocked migration to a modern ERP system. Operations were distributed across four custom legacy systems and paper-based processes dating back to the 1990s. A previous ERP migration project ran for four years, costing hundreds of thousands of euros, but failed.
By building on Odoo's standard manufacture-to-order workflows, Bryo delivered a fully integrated solution in just three months across all key modules: sales, manufacturing, shop floor, inventory, purchasing and invoicing. The key to this success was a deep understanding of the customers’ proprietary engineering tools and creating a simple connection to the Manufacturing module. This achieved a 20% efficiency gain in back-office operations within the first three months, alongside improved planning and delivery performance.
Attendees will learn how Odoo can successfully support complex engineer-to-order manufacturers, the importance of understanding customer-specific processes, and the implementation strategies that enabled a project previously considered too complex to become a successful digital transformation.
This session demonstrates how Odoo can become the backbone of even highly complex manufacturing operations when implemented with the right approach.
<div

tracks.title: Scaling a luxury retailer across five countries on Odoo
tracks.speaker: Ruben Van den broecke + Egbert Van Sande (DOL)
tracks.speaker_raw: Ruben Van den broecke + Egbert Van Sande (DOL), Project manager at Dynapps
tracks.speaker_bio: Senior Project manager at Dynapps, leading complex Odoo implementations in the Belgian and international markets.
tracks.description:
How do you grow a premium lifestyle brand across five countries, with Cuban cigars in one window and online auctions in the next, all running on a single platform?
That is the bet Dominique London is making. What started as a small shop in Ghent has grown into a multi-country retailer spanning Belgium, the UK, Switzerland, Luxembourg and the Canary Islands, with physical boutiques, a B2C webshop, a POS network, and a UK-grown online auction business. To support that ambition, the company chose Odoo as the single backbone for commerce, POS, inventory and accounting.
In this session, Dominique London and Dynapps share what it takes to make that work in practice. We zoom in on the architectural choices behind a multi-company, multi-country setup where one Odoo website automatically serves the right prices, products, VAT treatment and currency based on the visitor's location. We look at how strict assortment rules are handled at storefront and checkout level.
We also share the lessons that won't make the brochure: where standard Odoo simply works, where it doesn't, and which compromises pay off when you are racing toward a growth target.
Whether you run a multi-brand retailer, are about to launch in a second country, or are skeptical that a single ERP can carry both a luxury experience and a complex backend, this session gives you a practical look at how it is done.

tracks.title: One CRM, one source of truth: How a publishing company consolidated a fragmented customer landscape on Odoo – and powered its print-to-digital shift
tracks.speaker: Lars Schymonski from Ruhrdot
tracks.speaker_raw: Lars Schymonski from Ruhrdot
tracks.description:
media magneten, a publishing and advertising company in Essen, ran its sales on a fragmented landscape: SAP as the master-data backbone, a home-grown legacy system for orders and field service, and a scatter of point tools. Customer data lived everywhere and nowhere - no single view, constant manual re-entry between systems, and limited control over their own data. Together with ruhrdot., they made Odoo 19 the operational heart of the business: one CRM as the single source of truth for roughly 200,000 customer records, with SAP retained as the system of record. The result is a 360° customer view, sales workflows freed from manual re-entry and media breaks, advisor-specific marketing automation through Brevo, and trigger-based sales steering that tells advisors who to contact and when. Just as important, the project restored media magneten's sovereignty over its own customer data and laid the operational foundation for its strategic shift from print to digital. Instead of a big-bang cutover, ruhrdot. delivered a disciplined six-month MVP with a phased, pilot-first go-live. This talk shows how a mid-market company turns a CRM migration into a genuine business transformation.

tracks.title: From AI CPQ to Shop Floor: Connecting HIPE to Odoo for the Packaging Industry
tracks.speaker: Sébastien BOSSOUTROT
tracks.speaker_raw: Sébastien BOSSOUTROT, co-Founder and co-CEO at IROKOO
tracks.speaker_bio:
Co-presented by Sébastien Bossoutrot (IROKOO) and Thomas Othax (HIPE / Packitoo).
Sébastien Bossoutrot is co-founder and Co-CEO of IROKOO, one of France's leading Odoo Gold Partners.
An engineer who spent years working inside the packaging industry, he knows the trade from the shop floor up. Before IROKOO, he spent five years as an ERP project manager and pre-sales lead on a product vertical built for the packaging sector, bridging operations, business needs and software. A certified Odoo expert (v14 to v19) and functional architect, he now helps organizations turn Odoo into the operating system of their business.
Thomas Othax is the founder and CEO of Packitoo, a French software editor that aims to improve sales operations in the packaging industry.
Packitoo has developed HIPE, the first CPQ (Configure, Price, Quote) solution designed for the packaging industry, and is today launching a platform dedicated to creating AI agents for this sector.
Started in 2017, Packitoo has joined BOBST Group since 2024, one of the world’s leading suppliers of substrate processing, printing and converting equipment and services for the label, flexible packaging, folding carton and corrugated board industries.
tracks.description:
In the packaging industry, every order is unique. Dimensions, materials, printing, finishing: nothing is a standard catalog product. Yet most converters still quote these orders either in spreadsheets or in legacy ERPs that were never designed to handle configurable products. Margin only becomes clear after production. The configurator, when there is one, lives outside the ERP, so the gap between what was sold and what is produced gets filled manually, slowly, and with costly errors.
This talk shows, live in Odoo 19 (20), how an AI-powered CPQ built for packaging (HIPE) connects directly to Odoo to close that gap, end to end. HIPE owns the front of the funnel, configuration and AI-assisted quoting. The moment a quote is won, Odoo takes over the entire ERP backbone: the sales order, the cascading bill of materials, the purchase needs for materials and subcontracting, the manufacturing order, inventory, accounting, and a reliable cost, with no double entry. We walk the full path: from the configured quote in HIPE, to procurement and the shop floor, to inventory and margin analysis in Odoo.
We also share what it takes to make this integration reliable in real operations: keeping both systems in sync, handling errors gracefully, and turning a complex configured product into an accurate, multi-level bill of materials. Key takeaway: a concrete blueprint to turn Odoo into the backbone of configure-to-order manufacturing, with packaging as the showcase but lessons that apply to any made-to-order business.

The key takeaways for the audience will include how to identify domain gaps during discovery, avoid unnecessary over-customization, design freight workflows with long-term scalability, and build industry depth while preserving the flexibility of the Odoo platform. tracks.speaker_bio: Séphora Dayne Moreau is an Odoo Certified Consultant, founder and CEO of GS Conseils. With a Master’s Degree in Information Systems Integration Management and more than 15 years of experience in website development and digital transformation, she is passionate about turning business challenges into practical digital solutions. Her expertise spans business analysis, project management, website creation, and Odoo implementation.
tracks.description:
Toulet Medical is one of the medical equipment distributors on Réunion Island, a French overseas territory located in the Indian Ocean. The company serves healthcare professionals, medical institutions, care facilities, and private customers through multiple physical stores, warehouses, and complementary e-commerce websites.
Before Odoo, Toulet Medical relied on several separate solutions, including Sage for business management and accounting, PrestaShop for e-commerce, and additional tools used to support daily operations. As the company continued to grow, managing sales, inventory, purchasing, logistics, customer service, and online sales across multiple systems became increasingly complex, time-consuming, and costly.
To support its development, Toulet Medical decided to centralize its operations within Odoo and transform its information system into a single integrated platform. Today, Odoo is used to manage sales, purchasing, inventory, logistics, accounting, customer service, physical stores, and the Toulet Medical and Couches & Co e-commerce websites.
During this session, we will share the company’s digital transformation journey and explain how Odoo became the backbone of its operations.
Attendees will discover how the company successfully migrated from multiple disconnected applications to a unified ERP platform while preparing for future growth.
The presentation will also highlight the specific challenges of operating a medical equipment distribution company on Réunion Island, including import lead times, stock availability, multi-site operations, managing two brands and two e-commerce websites within the same company, multi-company environments, retail store operations, and the high level of customer service required in the healthcare sector.
Key Takeaways
* Successfully migrating from Sage and PrestaShop to Odoo.
* Centralizing sales, purchasing, inventory, accounting, and e-commerce within a single platform.
* Managing multiple stores and warehouses efficiently.
* Operating multiple e-commerce websites from a single database.
* Improving inventory visibility and replenishment processes.
* Supporting business growth through standardized and scalable processes.
* Lessons learned from a real-world implementation project on Réunion Island.
Value for the Audience
This session will provide a practical and transparent customer success story from a real-life digital transformation project. Participants will gain insights into the challenges encountered, the benefits achieved, and the lessons learned while replacing multiple business applications with a fully integrated ERP system.
Attendees will leave with concrete ideas and best practices that can be applied to their own organizations, whether they manage distribution operations, retail networks, e-commerce businesses, or multi-site companies.

tracks.title: Populate, Odoo's new data generation framework
tracks.speaker: Victor Piryns
tracks.speaker_raw: Victor Piryns, Performance Engineer at Odoo
tracks.speaker_bio: Victor Piryns is a performance engineer at Odoo. He works on improving performance across both Odoo’s core framework and business applications, as well as on tools that help developers analyze and test performance.
tracks.description:
Generating realistic Odoo databases for development, demonstrations, and performance testing has traditionally required custom scripts and considerable maintenance.

tracks.title: Scaling Odoo for Complex Retail: Dreambaby’s Journey Across 30+ Stores, a Central DC and Tailor-made applications
tracks.speaker: Daan Sileghem
tracks.speaker_role: Founder, Managing Partner at Konu BV
tracks.speaker_raw: Daan Sileghem, Founder, Managing Partner at Konu BV
tracks.speaker_bio: Daan Sileghem is the founder and one of two managing partners at Konu, an Odoo Partner based in Kortrijk, Belgium. With a strong background in sales and marketing, he quickly realised that true commercial success hinges on operational excellence. Driven by this insight, he helps companies untangle inefficient systems and streamline their operations with Odoo, bridging the gap between business needs and technical solutions.
tracks.description:
Dreambaby, the largest baby retail brand in Belgium, runs its core operation on Odoo. With more than 260 employees, 30+ physical stores (with additional stores planned for 2026), and a central warehouse, Odoo serves as the daily backbone for all core business processes.
The platform covers accounting, inventory, purchasing, sales, POS, HR, planning, attendance, customer service, and more, all within one centralised system. Despite numerous integrations with external systems, including marketing platforms, Shopify eCommerce, and Power BI, Odoo serves as the single source of truth (SSOT) for all operational and master data.
As Odoo partner Konu from Kortrijk, Belgium, we delivered the full implementation under a very ambitious timeline. Dreambaby migrated from SAP to Odoo and went live in just 8 months, followed by a hypercare phase of about 3 months, without disrupting ongoing operations.
While Odoo’s standard applications provided a strong foundation, Dreambaby’s retail-specific complexity required deep customisation across multiple core flows, including accounting, HR, POS, purchasing, sales, helpdesk, and more.
Inventory and logistics were heavily extended to match Dreambaby’s scale and complexity. Odoo manages 30+ stores in a multi-branch routing setup, with store replenishment driven by over one million replenishment rules. Store assortments are dynamically defined through a custom store range management application, powered by a bespoke sales forecasting tool. The platform supports advanced eCommerce flows, dynamic picking and prioritisation (for giftlists, online orders, and other channels), and online shipping directly from stores.
On top of the core platform, we developed a suite of custom-built applications tailored to Dreambaby’s business:
- A bespoke Giftlist (Birthlist) engine built in Odoo with a headless React frontend
- A custom loyalty program, deeply integrated with both POS and webshop
- A store replenishment engine with dynamic demand forecasting
- Automated shelf label printing driven by real-time pricing
- A dynamic price display system for managing in-store and online promotions
Today, we continue to support Dreambaby on a daily basis, driving its ongoing digital transformation with fast-paced improvements to the giftlist, loyalty program, and overall shop concept. This is an ongoing journey, part of a broader conceptual modernisation of the Dreambaby retail experience. The roadmap focuses on evolving the tailor-made applications and strengthening employee-facing tools and interfaces, with a clear emphasis on improving both customer and employee experiences.
This session offers an honest and practical account of the project: what worked well, where we encountered friction, and what we would approach differently. It is ideal for teams considering Odoo for full operational coverage in a complex retail environment.

tracks.speaker_raw: Nico Ziemski from ruhrdot GmbH
tracks.description:
Zeitgeist GmbH runs four consumer lifestyle brands (the watch brands Detomaso, Yves Camani and Lilienthal plus Kooja) across direct-to-consumer Shopify stores and the Amazon and Otto marketplaces, with e-commerce as the group's core business. Their legacy Sage ERP modeled stock as components and bills of materials, which created a constant overselling risk and tied up a large block of component inventory that blocked a clean transition. ruhrdot. replaced Sage with a single Odoo 19 Enterprise instance for the entire group: two legal entities in one multi-company setup, a simplified single-SKU inventory model, and separate DATEV exports per entity for German accounting compliance. Odoo sits at the hub of the supply chain, orchestrating four Shopify stores through a custom connector, the Amazon and Otto channels through a middleware, and fulfillment through third-party logistics via a SOAP integration that also routes watch engraving. Instead of a big-bang cutover, we went live brand by brand, month by month, so learnings from the first brand fed the next. This talk shows how to design a multi-brand group ERP from day one, retire a risky legacy inventory model, and de-risk a large migration through phased go-lives.

tracks.title: Odev meets AI : Automating Odoo development end-to-end
tracks.speaker: Sébastien Andreatta from Odoo
tracks.speaker_raw: Sébastien Andreatta from Odoo
tracks.description:
odev is the CLI Odoo developers already reach for daily: it spins up a database on any Odoo version, manages worktrees and git branches per task, handles venvs and dependencies, runs the server, runs the tests, and generally removes the boilerplate around working with Odoo source. What it didn't do — until now — is write the code for you.
This talk shows how we plugged AI agents (Claude Code, Gemini CLI, Copilot, OpenCode) directly into that existing workflow. Instead of bolting AI on as a separate tool, odev uses the environment it already manages — the right Odoo version, the right worktree, a running database — as the context an AI agent needs to actually get work done: analyzing a task, scaffolding the module, running it, testing it, and iterating against real failures instead of hallucinated ones.
We'll do a live, end-to-end demo: starting from a bare task description, watch odev set up the dev environment and hand it off to an AI agent that scaffolds, runs, and tests a real Odoo module — then talk through what worked, what broke, and the design decisions behind wiring AI into a tool developers already trust for the unglamorous plumbing of Odoo development.

tracks.description:
Odoo does not use explicit accounting entries to pass account balances from period to period. Some reports (typically the Balance Sheet) therefore need to recompute such balances dynamically every time from the whole history. As the size of the accounting grows in time, this can become a bottleneck for performance, as there are more and more entries to consider.
For years, Odoo has been living without solution to this problem ; not anymore !
Odoo 20 introduces a new automatic caching mechanism for accounting reports. This talk will explain how it works, what it does, and how to use it.

tracks.title: Beyond the Website Builder: Building Headless and Custom Interfaces on Odoo
tracks.speaker: Guillaume Roisin
tracks.speaker_raw: Guillaume Roisin, CEO at Sigmagency SRL
tracks.speaker_bio: Guillaume Roisin is the founder of Sigmagency, a digital transformation partner specializing in Odoo and advanced web development. With a background as a civil engineer in applied mathematics, Guillaume combines deep technical expertise with a human-centered approach to digital projects. He started building websites as a freelancer in university and quickly expanded after graduating into Odoo to offer integrated, scalable solutions for SMEs looking to modernize their operations. Passionate about problem-solving and process optimization, Guillaume helps companies connect their ERP, websites, and custom applications into unified ecosystems that drive growth, efficiency, and innovation.
tracks.description:
Summary
Most companies treat Odoo as a back-office and stop there. But Odoo is also the backend behind every interface your customers, partners and field teams actually touch custom portals, headless web and mobile apps, even offline-first tools for people working with no connection.
For years these architectures were expensive and reserved for ambitious projects. AI just changed the economics: the plumbing is cheap now, so far more projects can justify a custom front-end on top of Odoo. But the hard part didn't disappear it moved. The challenge is no longer can you build it, it's can you architect it so your data stays trustworthy.
In this talk we'll show what's possible beyond the standard Odoo website, when to go custom versus when to stay standard, and the architecture rules that keep one source of truth no matter how custom the interface gets with real examples in production.
Description
The standard Odoo website is excellent, and for most projects it should be the default. But some businesses need more than a theme can deliver: a customer portal with bespoke workflows, a native mobile app, a public platform at scale, or a tool their field teams can use with no internet at all.
The usual reflex is to bolt on a separate system and instantly recreate the data silos and manual reconciliation everyone is trying to escape. There's a better way: keep Odoo as the single source of truth for orders, inventory, accounting and CRM, and build the interface as a headless front-end that talks to Odoo as its backend. The result is a best-in-class user experience and full operational integration, you no longer have to choose.
What's new in 2026 is the economics. AI collapses the cost of the plumbing: the boilerplate, the API glue, the type generation from Odoo models, the sync scaffolding. Projects that weren't viable two years ago are viable today, and the market for custom interfaces is expanding fast. But that's also the trap: far more teams will now attempt these architectures without knowing where the landmines are. AI answers "can you build it." It does not answer "can you architect it so the data stays reliable." That judgment is the whole game.
In clear, practical terms, we'll cover:
The decision framework : how to tell whether a project belongs on the standard Odoo website or warrants a custom/headless interface, and the honest trade-offs in cost, time and maintainability. Standard should win more often than you'd think.
Odoo as a backend, not just a back-office : treating Odoo's data and business logic as the API core for any interface, so there's one source of truth no matter how custom the front-end gets.
Three faces of the custom front-end, one Odoo backend : the customer-facing product at scale (a headless platform serving 200k+ catalog items on Odoo), the partner/bespoke portal (custom React front-ends), and the hardest one: the offline-first field tool, where agents work with no connection, with sync and conflict resolution feeding everything straight back into Odoo.
The rules that keep it sane : where business logic must live (in Odoo, never in the front-end), how to handle auth, performance, offline sync and data integrity. The exact rules AI makes more critical, not less.
What this unlocks for your business : bespoke customer and partner experiences, mobile and field operations, and ambitious digital products, while every transaction still flows straight into Odoo.
By the end, you'll know what Odoo is truly capable of as the backbone of any digital product, when to stay standard and when to go custom and why, in the AI era, the value has shifted from writing the code to architecting it right.

tracks.title: Automated Data Exports and External Integrations
tracks.speaker: CRETU Victor
tracks.speaker_raw: CRETU Victor, Business Analyst at Sodexis SAS
tracks.speaker_bio: Victor CRETU est business analyste et travaille chez Sodexis depuis 2 ans. Il a une expérience de 6 ans à l'utilisation de Odoo. Il a accompagné beaucoup d'entreprises de différentes tailles dans leur implémentation de Odoo.
tracks.description:
For Map Space Coating, data fluidity between enterprise systems and external tools is crucial for effective project management. However, the daily routine of manually filtering, exporting, and distributing data files from their ERP was tedious and prone to delays. By implementing a tailored Automated Export solution within Odoo, Map Space Coating streamlined their data extraction process.
The Challenge: Friction in Data Portability
Before standardizing their automated export process, Map Space Coating faced several operational roadblocks:
- Manual Export Fatigue: Team members had to log into Odoo daily, navigate to specific modules, apply complex filters, and manually download files.
- External Tool Bottlenecks: Project managers heavily rely on specialized external tools for advanced analysis and planning. Delays in manually exporting data from Odoo meant delays in updating these crucial external systems.
- Inconsistent Data Retrieval: Depending on who was performing the export, different filters might be accidentally applied, leading to inconsistent datasets being shared with project managers.
The Odoo Solution
To eliminate these inefficiencies, a robust, scheduled export automation was developed within Odoo. The solution was designed to act as a reliable bridge between Odoo and external tools.
1. Advanced & Flexible Filtering
- Dynamic Filter Application: The automated export engine is programmed to respect and utilize Odoo's standard, by-default filters.
- "Favorites" Integration: More importantly, the system can seamlessly draw from "Favorite" (custom-saved) filters created by users. This means project managers can define their exact data requirements once via the Odoo UI, save it as a favorite, and the automated system will apply that precise logic to all future exports.
2. Daily Automated Scheduling
To ensure data is always fresh and ready for external tools, the manual click-to-export process was completely bypassed.
- Scheduled Actions (Cron Jobs): Odoo was configured with automated scheduled actions that trigger on a daily basis.
- Zero-Touch Generation: Without any human intervention, the system runs the pre-defined queries, compiles the data, and generates the necessary export files (e.g., CSV or Excel) formatted perfectly for Map Space Coating's external tools.
3. Direct Delivery to Project Managers
Generating the file automatically is only half the solution; delivering it is the other.
- Automated Routing: Once the daily file is generated, the Odoo solution automatically drafts an email and attaches the exported file.
- Targeted Communication: The email is instantly dispatched to the specific Project Manager overseeing that data set. When the PM starts their workday, the exact data they need to import into their external tools is already waiting in their inbox.
Key Benefits and Results
The implementation of this automated export feature delivered immediate value to Map Space Coating's daily operations:
- Significant Time Savings: Administrative staff and project managers no longer waste time on repetitive manual data extraction, freeing them up for higher-value tasks.
- Guaranteed Data Consistency: By relying on saved "favorite" filters, the exported data structure remains 100% consistent every single day, preventing errors during external tool imports.
- Seamless External Integration: Project managers now have a frictionless workflow. The daily delivery of precise data files ensures their external project management and analysis tools are always up-to-date.
Conclusion
By automating the file export process in Odoo, Map Space Coating has successfully broken down data silos between their ERP and external tools. This automated, daily routine ensures that project managers are consistently equipped with the accurate, up-to-date information they need, saving time and significantly boosting overall operational efficiency.

tracks.speaker_bio: Guillaume Roisin is the founder of Sigmagency, a digital transformation partner specializing in Odoo and advanced web development. With a background as a civil engineer in applied mathematics, Guillaume combines deep technical expertise with a human-centered approach to digital projects. He started building websites as a freelancer in university and quickly expanded after graduating into Odoo to offer integrated, scalable solutions for SMEs looking to modernize their operations. Passionate about problem-solving and process optimization, Guillaume helps companies connect their ERP, websites, and custom applications into unified ecosystems that drive growth, efficiency, and innovation.
tracks.description:
SUMMARY
Most agencies build websites and e-commerce platforms disconnected from business operations, forcing companies to manage data in silos.
In this talk, we will explain why using Odoo as the backbone for websites and e-commerce ecosystems is the best way to scale while reducing manual work and operational complexity. We will share what this shift means for your business and how it can transform your digital presence into a growth engine.
DESCRIPTION
Your website should do more than just look good. It should connect seamlessly with your operations, eliminate manual processes, and help your business scale.
Most companies use separate systems for their website, e-commerce, CRM, and accounting, forcing teams to re-enter orders, manage inventory manually, and reconcile data across platforms. This fragmentation creates inefficiencies, errors, and wasted resources that slow growth.
Using Odoo as the backbone for your website and e-commerce changes the game. In this talk, we will explain in clear business terms:
Why building websites and e-commerce on Odoo reduces friction between sales, finance, and operations while delivering a seamless customer experience.
How using Odoo allows us to design beautiful, high-converting websites without sacrificing the operational power and reporting you need to grow.
How this approach automates order management, invoicing, inventory, and customer communication directly from your website or e-commerce portal.
Why an Odoo-based architecture makes scaling your online business easier while reducing dependency on costly integrations.
How headless and advanced UI/UX strategies can still be applied while keeping Odoo as your operational core.
At Sigmagency, we experienced this first-hand. As a web agency, we built high-converting websites, but our clients struggled with fragmented tools. This led us to transition into a full-stack Odoo partner, helping SMEs connect their websites, e-commerce, and back-office processes into a single, scalable ecosystem.
Throughout this talk, we will share concrete examples of SMEs that have scaled their online services by building Odoo-powered websites connected directly to their CRM, accounting, and inventory. These examples will show how integrated ecosystems help companies sell more while working less, demonstrating the unique advantage of leveraging Odoo’s full potential.
By the end of this session, you will understand how Odoo can align your online sales channels with your operations, enabling your company to scale sustainably while improving customer satisfaction.

Sodexis has been a dedicated, full-service Odoo Implementation Partner since 2012, continuously innovating its development and optimization strategies to maximize customer ROI and user experience. With extensive expertise gained over 175+ successful projects and hundreds of custom applications, Sodexis developed the FreightView Connector to seamlessly extend Odoo Enterprise environments into robust, enterprise-grade freight management systems.

tracks.description:
50% Faster Quotes & 90% Fewer Errors: A Practical Approach to Configure-to-Order CPQ (Custom Product Configurator) in Odoo
Custom and configure-to-order manufacturers all face the same hard problem: every quote is unique, the number of possible product combinations runs into the thousands, and a single wrong attribute can flow all the way to the shop floor as a costly error. Many teams still handle this complexity manually, which is slow, fragile, and hard to scale.
This session walks through a practical, reusable approach to configure-to-order CPQ in Odoo, drawn from real configure-to-order implementations. We will cover how to structure product attributes and variants so the configurator stays manageable instead of exploding, how to drive accurate bills of materials straight from the configured quote, and how Aktiv’s Odoo CPQ solution enables you for this transformation. Across these implementations, the approach has cut quoting time by roughly half and reduced configuration errors by up to 90% by removing manual rework.
With our live demonstration, attendees will learn how to:
- Configure complex products with dynamic pricing rules
- Handle complex scenarios with custom dimensions using Parametric Configuration
- Automate proposal generation and streamline approval workflows
- Enhance customer satisfaction with accurate and timely product configurations
- Optimize manufacturing workflows with dynamic Bill Of Materials (BoM)
- Leverage the integration with Odoo Sales, Purchase, Inventory & Manufacturing modules for a unified solution
Join us at Odoo Experience 2026 to discover how Odoo CPQ can transform your sales and manufacturing operations, improve efficiency, and drive growth in your business.

tracks.title: A Safe Blueprint to Migrate your SaaS Billing to Odoo
tracks.speaker: Tomás Van Loock
tracks.speaker_raw: Tomás Van Loock, ERP Consultant at much. Consulting
tracks.speaker_bio: Tomás Van Loock is an AI & BI ERP Consultant at much. Consulting. Combining a background in Data Science and Management, he approaches Odoo Enterprise as a unified ecosystem rather than a collection of siloed applications. His implementation portfolio spans Manufacturing, Field Service, and eCommerce architectures. This broad horizontal system expertise allows him to bypass module constraints and map intricate business requirements into natively integrated Odoo frameworks.
tracks.description:
Fast-scaling B2B SaaS platforms often face a critical dilemma: their external subscription billing engine operates separately from their financial backbone, forcing accounting teams to manually reconcile thousands of fragmented transactions. If the business now reorganises internal processes, moving all at once to a new ERP system is risky. In that situation, consultants need to find a way to link the existing and new systems without disrupting everyday work.
Instead of forcing a high-risk immediate transition, we designed a phased integration strategy anchored directly in Odoo Accounting. y configuring a controlled, on-demand synchronization workflow via API, we bypassed the unpredictability of real-time webhooks, giving the finance team absolute control to pull, construct, and fully reconcile multi-currency invoices, payments, and credit notes securely within Odoo's standard accounting models.
This strategic phase-one deployment eliminated manual cross-system data entry entirely, guaranteeing absolute financial accuracy across the organization. As a direct result, the automated workflow instantly reduced the monthly financial close from 15 days down to 5, buying the client the operational stability required to systematically plan their eventual phase-two migration into native Odoo Subscriptions.
Key Points of this Talk:
- Executing a phased integration strategy to stabilize operations during internal organizational flux.
- Unifying external subscription billing data directly with Odoo Enterprise Accounting models.
- Automating multi-currency invoice creation and payment reconciliation to eliminate manual entry.
- Bypassing complex real-time webhooks in favor of highly controlled, on-demand financial synchronizations.
- Securing absolute accounting veridicality across disconnected systems before a full ERP migration.
- Reducing the financial close from 15 days to 5 days on the first execution.
Key Learnings:
- How to evaluate a phased custom integration strategy vs. an immediate full platform migration.
- How to map external subscription lifecycle states to standard Odoo Enterprise financial workflows.
- How to mitigate project risk by delivering immediate operational ROI before proposing system-wide migrations.
- How to give finance teams control over data synchronizations without relying on volatile push notifications.
- How to utilize temporary external connectors as a strategic stepping stone toward Odoo Subscriptions.

Functional Consultants, Project Managers, and Finance Directors.

tracks.title: Odoo Has Eyes: Connecting Smart Cameras and Sensors to Your ERP
tracks.speaker: Alexander De Waele
tracks.speaker_raw: Alexander De Waele, Managing Partner at Konu BV
tracks.speaker_bio:
Alexander De Waele has a Masters degree in electromechanics specialized in automation, with more than fifteen years of experience in operational management and technical management roles at several large companies.
He is now managing partner and co-owner of Konu, a Belgian Odoo partner focused on pragmatic ERP implementations for medium-sized and large companies, as well as ambitious startups and scale-ups that want to grow quickly and innovate.
His background in engineering and operational management gives him a practical view on ERP projects: not only how systems should be configured, but how they need to work in real daily operations. He is especially interested in using Odoo as a platform that connects business processes with external systems, hardware, operational data and real-world events.
tracks.description:
Odoo is already a powerful platform for managing sales, inventory, accounting, POS, manufacturing and many other business processes. But in many companies, valuable operational data is still captured outside Odoo: by cameras, sensors, machines, counters or other external devices.
In this talk, we present Komeet, a project developed at Konu to connect intelligent cameras and external sensors with Odoo. The use case we will focus on is automatic visitor counting in a retail context. Instead of relying on manual estimates or separate analytics tools, a smart camera counts the number of visitors entering a store and sends that information to Odoo.
Using practical examples, we will show how this kind of integration can create value: combining visitor data with POS results, measuring conversion rates, improving staffing decisions, following up store performance or exploring similar use cases in logistics, manufacturing and service environments. The session is meant to inspire Odoo partners, developers and business users to think of Odoo as a platform connected to the physical world.

tracks.description:
18 years. 382 international matches. European, World and Olympic titles.
An 18-year journey at the highest level of international hockey, as part of the Belgian Red Lions and their historic transformation from a second-tier hockey nation into the world’s number one team.
This journey was about far more than sporting talent. It was about building a shared ambition, creating a strong team culture, developing trust and accountability, raising standards, embracing setbacks and learning how to perform together under pressure.
The Red Lions spirit: a winning culture and high team performance How does a team transform from a second-tier nation into the number one team in the world?
This keynote takes the audience behind the Red Lions’ journey and explores the principles that enabled this transformation: a clear vision, a shared purpose, high standards, resilience, trust and collective accountability.
The lessons of elite sport go far beyond the hockey field. They provide powerful insights into leadership, teamwork, culture and sustainable performance — and into what it takes to turn ambition into consistent collective success.

tracks.description:
Real estate operations often stall when data must manually transition between disconnected tools during a property’s lifecycle. Fragmented systems complicate everything from vendor onboarding and automated buyer matching to fee calculations and rental contract management.
This session demonstrates how the Real Estate Agency and Property Management modules unify these steps into a single, continuous workflow.
We will explore how a new property listing automatically triggers subscriber matching, routes inbound marketplace leads into a structured nurturing pipeline equipped with visit scheduling and offer shortcuts, and seemlessly calculates commission fees. tracks.title: Measure, snap, quote, note: Digitize your field operations with Odoo
tracks.speaker: Mathieu Herbos from Odoo
tracks.speaker_raw: Mathieu Herbos from Odoo
tracks.speaker_bio: Mathieu Herbos is a Business Development Representative at Odoo Belgium, where he helps SMEs from a wide range of industries digitize their operations. He works daily with sales and field teams to design workflows that fit real-life use cases.
tracks.description:
A large part of an SME's sales activity happens outside the office: at the client's home, in a showroom, on the road. The data created there is where deals are won or lost, but it often gets stuck between a notebook, a phone gallery and a WhatsApp thread before it ever reaches the CRM.
In this talk, we follow the real-life journey of a kitchen designer and fitter, from the first lead to the signed order. A prospect fills in a form on the website, a salesperson qualifies the lead and books a home visit, takes measurements and photos on site, builds the quotation on the tablet with product variants and options, and gets the client to sign on the spot.
Along the way, we'll show how CRM and Sales, combined with Odoo's mobile experience, help SMEs shorten their sales cycle, close deals on-site, and make sure no lead ever gets lost between the showroom and the field.
